events.text: The isle has drifted a finger's width since you sat down on it. The moss on your knees is older than the kingdom you were born in.

choices.text: Brush the moss from your knees and leave it be

effects.log: You wipe a patch clear and the moss grows back by evening. The two of you reach an understanding.

choices.text: Measure the finger's width with a hair

effects.log: The hair confirms it. You tie the hair to a pine twig, a small flag for the next age.

events.text: Rain has fallen on this isle eleven times in the years you have sat here. You counted each. The twelfth is coming up the cloud-slope now.

choices.text: Count the twelfth rain with the first eleven

effects.log: Twelve small rains, twelve small clearings in the mind. You write the number on the eave.

choices.text: Sit out in the twelfth rain unsheltered

effects.log: It beads on your shoulders and runs off in lines. You rise lighter, and the cushion is dry beneath you.

choices.text: Fetch a bowl and keep the rain

effects.log: You steep next month's tea in it. It tastes of the long sitting.

events.text: A stone-pine on the rim of your isle was a seedling when you arrived. It has outgrown your roof and begun to lean over you like an elder.

choices.text: Trim the stone-pine away from your roof

effects.log: A kind of betrayal, and the pine sulks for a season. The roof, though, lets in the stars again.

choices.text: Let the pine lean, and learn its patience

effects.log: You sit under it a month. Its slowness is the right size for yours.

choices.text: Hang a lantern from its oldest branch

effects.log: It glows through the night. Passing immortals take it for a shrine, and leave small offerings.

events.text: Your isle has crossed the whole width of the Sea of Clouds once and is turning back. You never rose from the cushion to watch it go.

choices.text: Rise at last and watch the isle turn back

effects.log: It takes a morning. The far shore is exactly as you left it. You sit down again, and the sitting is the richer.

choices.text: Stay seated and trust the cushion

effects.log: The crossing goes on without you. Something in you is turning too, and you let it.

events.text: Whole houses were founded, quarrelled and dissolved on the isles below you while you breathed. Their ghost-lanterns still drift up past your window.

choices.text: Light a lantern for the dissolved houses

effects.log: It drifts up with the others. You feel briefly like the keeper of a very quiet graveyard.

choices.text: Study why those houses failed

effects.log: Hurry, mostly. You note it down without smugness.

choices.text: Close the window and sit on

effects.log: The ghost-lanterns pass unregarded. You breathe until the room is dark and even.

events.text: Some mornings the settling is nothing but weight: as if the cushion were the isle, and the isle the sky, and you the only thing holding it down.

choices.text: Let yourself be the weight

effects.log: You stop holding up the sky and let the sky hold you. The cushion eases.

choices.text: Lift your hands from your knees and feel the air

effects.log: A thin cool gap. The weight is real, and so is the lightness under it.

choices.text: Ask the isle quietly to bear a little more

effects.log: Foolish, maybe. The floor hums once, as if amused.

events.text: The tea in your cup has long since stopped being the point. You sit with it anyway, and the steam draws the same slow curl every dawn.

choices.text: Drink the tea as it is, cold or warm

effects.log: It is cold. You drink it all and the cup feels fuller than it was.

choices.text: Watch the steam curl till it forgets itself

effects.log: The curl and the mind unwind together. Your qi rides the same slow spiral.

events.text: Your foundation has deepened so slowly that you cannot tell the day it changed. You only know the old stillness, when it comes, is very much larger.

choices.text: Mark today on the wall with a small stroke

effects.log: One stroke among thousands. You cannot say what makes today different, only that you wished to witness it.

choices.text: Test the new stillness with a deliberate noise

effects.log: A cough, a clap. It sinks into the quiet and does not come back. Remarkable.

choices.text: Do not test it, and just be in it

effects.log: You leave the stillness unexamined, like a sleeping cat. It stays.

events.text: Centuries pass in single breaths now. A messenger bird that came to your gate as a chick has taken three mates and been buried under the plum tree.

choices.text: Bury the messenger bird's last feather by the plum

effects.log: You give it a short word. The plum will bloom white this year, you are sure.

choices.text: Read the mail the new birds bring

effects.log: Dull, mostly, with one line of real news. Centuries mean little to a postmaster.

choices.text: Send no answer, and let the birds nest

effects.log: A small noisy family takes your eave. The breath goes on through the chirping.

events.text: At this height the settling feels less like waiting than like being slowly set into the sky itself, a stone in a wall that nobody sees but the wall.

choices.text: Be the stone in the wall

effects.log: You let go of looking out. The wall is the sky and the stone is you. Nothing is lacking.

choices.text: Look out once, to see the wall from the front

effects.log: A faint seam of cloud, a faint seam of you. Then it closes again.

events.text: You lay your palm on the gate above you, as you do each new moon. It is cold and smooth as a lake in winter, and it does not so much as hum.

choices.text: Warm your hand on the stone of the isle first, then touch the gate

effects.log: The gate is the same. Your hand, warmer, notices a faint grain it missed.

choices.text: Leave the gate for the next moon, and pour tea

effects.log: A lesser ritual, kept. The moon will be back, and so will you.

events.text: The gate is there. You can feel its hinges. You can feel its lock. What you cannot feel is the key, and you have begun to suspect it is not something you carry.

choices.text: Go looking for the key in your past

effects.log: You list what you have carried. Everything you find is a weight, not a key.

choices.text: Look for the key outside yourself, in the Scroll Hall

effects.log: A librarian points you to nothing in particular and wishes you luck. It is something to have asked.

choices.text: Stop looking for it

effects.log: The pressure lifts a hair. The gate has not changed, but your search has.

events.text: Three times you have thrown yourself at the gate and three times it has handed you back unchanged, like a door that politely refuses a gift.

choices.text: Count your three failed throws as three lessons

effects.log: Hard, flat, fair. You can list what each one told you, and the list is a path.

choices.text: Try a gentler fourth: lean, not throw

effects.log: The gate gives a slight, almost courteous, resistance. You learn the pressure it prefers.

choices.text: Admit you were showing off, and bow to it

effects.log: The bow feels like the first honest thing in a decade.

events.text: Somewhere above the clouds a bell rings for a rung you have not reached. You hear it every dusk, and every dusk you answer by sitting straighter.

choices.text: Climb in your mind toward the bell

effects.log: You rise through the cold, nearer, nearer, then lose the sound. It leaves a taste of brass.

choices.text: Hum the bell's note yourself at dusk

effects.log: The hum steadies you. For a breath the gate hums back.

choices.text: Sit straighter and say nothing

effects.log: A plain answer to a plain call. The back remembers it.

events.text: The gate leans in the dark of your inner sight like a cliff with no hold anywhere on it. Others have climbed it. Their ropes are still hanging.

choices.text: Study the hanging ropes of the ones who failed

effects.log: Every rope is cut at the same height. You mark the height and keep it in mind.

choices.text: Add your own rope, then take it down

effects.log: It is a ritual of letting be. The cliff stays a cliff, and you stay at its foot, content.

events.text: You have started to talk to the gate. Mostly nonsense. Last night you thanked it for being so thorough, and felt, absurdly, that it was pleased.

choices.text: Thank it again, and mean the second thank-you more

effects.log: The gate says nothing, but the dark seems warmer. A queer friendship.

choices.text: Ask it how long you must wait

effects.log: Silence, of course. But the silence has a length, and you note it.

choices.text: Tell it your plan, in detail

effects.log: It listens to all of it. When you finish you have heard the plan for the first time, and mend it.

events.text: The gate is not locked, you realise, so much as unfinished: a door someone began and never hung. The work of hanging it is yours.

choices.text: Begin hanging the door, one hinge at a time

effects.log: You work at it nightly. It is more like carpentry than conquest, and you rather like it.

choices.text: Ask who left it unfinished

effects.log: No one answers. A fragment of an old builder's patience settles in you instead.

choices.text: Rest from the door and mend your own tools first

effects.log: Your inner breath is rough in spots. A month of sanding makes the later carpentry easy.

events.text: Every method says push. Every method is written by someone who got through, and who therefore cannot tell you what the gate was doing before they pushed.

choices.text: Do the opposite: wait, and watch what it does

effects.log: At dusk the gate breathes in, very faintly. You time it, and your own breath joins.

choices.text: Write to the authors who got through

effects.log: Two reply. Both say the same thing in different words, and you take comfort in the agreement.

choices.text: Push, as the methods say, and see for yourself

effects.log: The method fails at your depth and says why. You lose a night and gain a page.

events.text: At this height the gate has no surface at all. You press, and your hand goes in to the wrist, into a calm that asks nothing, and that is the difficulty.

choices.text: Draw your hand back from the calm

effects.log: It is not retreat. The calm stays on your wrist like water, and you carry it to bed.

choices.text: Go in to the elbow

effects.log: A vast, level patience takes the arm. It asks nothing, and you give it nothing, and that nothing is real.

choices.text: Say aloud what you need

effects.log: Four words. The calm does not answer, but it does make room.

events.text: The last gate is nearly a thing without a shape. You lean toward it each night and each night find only the same wide patient dark, waiting for you to need less.

choices.text: Need less, as an exercise: one thing a night

effects.log: You relinquish a habit a night. By the hundredth, the dark waits less.

choices.text: Lean in and keep leaning

effects.log: Leaning is a posture without a goal. You hold it until dawn.

choices.text: Turn your back to it and sit with the stars

effects.log: Courtesy to the gate and to yourself. The dark is behind you, patient as a pond.

events.text: You failed at the gate, and the failure has the shape of a fist-sized hole in your qi that fills a little each day. Today it filled enough to look inside.

choices.text: Look into the hole and name its shape

effects.log: It is the shape of a hand that grabbed. You decide to practise opening it.

choices.text: Wait for it to fill without looking

effects.log: A kind of patience. It fills by season's end, a touch richer.

events.text: The attempt ended in a roar of lightning and a long silence. You have gone over that silence a hundred times, and tonight you hear what it was saying.

choices.text: Listen to the silence again, with a pencil

effects.log: You draw it as a line, a breath, a gap. The gap is where the lesson is.

choices.text: Ask the silence what it wants

effects.log: It wants you to hurry less, it turns out. Obvious and unwelcome.

choices.text: Leave the silence alone

effects.log: Some silences are best kept for later. This one will wait.

events.text: A rival's last attempt failed too, they tell you, in much the same way. You find that a poor comfort, and a surprisingly good map.

choices.text: Visit the rival and compare the failures

effects.log: Two cups, two scorings. You see the pattern, and the rival sees it in you.

choices.text: Keep the comfort to yourself and your own map

effects.log: A small, private ledger. The map is clearer for being unshared.

events.text: What broke was not the foundation. It was your pride, bolted over the foundation so long that you mistook it for stone.

choices.text: Unbolt the pride, plank by plank

effects.log: It is sorrier work than you thought. Beneath it the foundation has been waiting, unharmed.

choices.text: Leave the pride and reinforce it

effects.log: Foolish, and it feels fine for a while. Then it creaks.

choices.text: Show the pride to a trusted friend

effects.log: They laugh, kindly, and carry half the load for an afternoon.

events.text: You replay the failed attempt one breath at a time, like a painting seen through a slit. Eleventh breath: there. A flinch. You had flinched.

choices.text: Go back to the eleventh breath and feel the flinch

effects.log: Slow. Terrible. You find the flinch is a memory of an old blow, long healed.

choices.text: Rehearse the attempt without flinching

effects.log: In the dark, a hundred times. Your body begins to forget the old fear.

choices.text: Forgive the flinch

effects.log: It is a small gift to yourself. The painting, seen again, is less sharp, and clearer.

events.text: The healers of the Nine Clouds say the injury is nearly mended. They do not say the other thing, the thing in the account of the attempt, which you now say aloud.

choices.text: Say the thing aloud to the healers

effects.log: They say nothing. One touches your wrist, briefly. It helps more than advice.

choices.text: Say it aloud to the empty room

effects.log: The room takes it in. A tension in the shoulders departs.

events.text: The storm came as it always does and you met it as you always had. That was the error: it was a new storm, and you answered it with an old self.

choices.text: Study the new storm as a stranger

effects.log: You make notes, as on any unfamiliar weather. Next time you will not answer a stranger as an old friend.

choices.text: Bury the old self with a small rite

effects.log: A cup of tea on the soil. The self is not gone, but it is no longer in charge.

events.text: Failure at this height has no witnesses. That makes it purer, and harder. Only you can say what went wrong, and you have been avoiding the sentence for years.

choices.text: Say the sentence at last

effects.log: It is shorter than you feared, and quite ordinary. The years of avoidance fall away like an old coat.

choices.text: Write the sentence and lock it in a box

effects.log: A start. The box is heavy with it, and the room, lighter.

choices.text: Let a friend say it first

effects.log: They have known for a century. They say it kindly, and it is not the worst.

events.text: You pour a cup for the self that stood at the gate just before it failed. You are surprised how little anger there is in the pouring.

choices.text: Pour a second cup for your better self

effects.log: You drink the first. The second cools, and you leave it by the window as an offering.

choices.text: Thank the self for trying

effects.log: It is awkward at first, then natural. The ache in the chest eases.

events.text: A failed attempt at this height is mostly a long listening. You listen, and in the quiet beneath the ringing you find the single thread that pulled.

choices.text: Follow the thread that pulled

effects.log: It leads back, and back, to a certain morning in your youth. You understand it, and set it down.

choices.text: Cut the thread and weave a new one

effects.log: A long labour, humble, exact. The weave holds.

choices.text: Listen longer, and ask nothing

effects.log: The ringing quiets, and you hear the room, the sea, the stars. That is the lesson of the day.

events.text: Tonight the air thickens. The sea of clouds under your isle goes quiet in a way you have not heard before, a held breath the width of a province.

choices.text: Close your eyes and listen to the whole province hold its breath

effects.log: You join it. For an hour the world and you are of one size.

choices.text: Break the quiet with a single clear note

effects.log: A bell, a flute, a hum. The sea of clouds answers faintly, and the hush becomes a duet.

events.text: Your senses sharpen to a painful clarity. You can hear dew forming. In the distance a bird turns its head, and you can hear that too.

choices.text: Turn the clarity inward and listen to your own dew

effects.log: You hear your qi form droplets on the inside of the golden core. They are beautiful.

choices.text: Dull your senses a little, for rest

effects.log: A kindly act. Tomorrow's clarity will be fresher for the sleep.

events.text: You have arranged everything: the array, the pills, the wards. And still the thing that matters is the thing that cannot be arranged, which is you.

choices.text: Put the arrangements down and sit with the part that cannot be arranged

effects.log: It is only you. You find you are better company than you feared.

choices.text: Add one more ward, just in case

effects.log: It does not matter, and you will sleep a little better.

choices.text: Burn the list of pills

effects.log: A gesture. The pills remain, but the list was the fear.

events.text: The stars have gone out one by one on the side of the sky where the gate lies. Not a storm yet. The courtesy before a storm.

choices.text: Say good evening to the dark side of the sky

effects.log: A faint star blinks back. The courtesy is returned.

choices.text: Look away, to the stars that remain

effects.log: You count the ones left. Every one is a friend, and you take a long look at each.

events.text: A single drop of rain falls on your cushion, then nothing. The wind drops. Every leaf on the stone-pine hangs still, listening for you.

choices.text: Take the drop on your palm and wait with the pine

effects.log: The two of you wait. When the first leaf stirs, you stir, and the wait is over.

choices.text: Wipe the cushion and sit down on the dry corner

effects.log: Practical, steadying. Tomorrow will be wet enough.

events.text: Old companions have sent word that they will watch from the next isle. You are touched, and a little irritated, and mostly glad.

choices.text: Wave to the next isle and invite them over

effects.log: A pot of tea, three guests, and the eve is no longer lonely.

choices.text: Send word that you prefer to sit alone

effects.log: They understand. A candle on the next isle burns all night, in sympathy.

choices.text: Write them each one line of thanks

effects.log: Short, true, nearly shy. You sleep the better for it.

events.text: The eve is a long hush, and in it you review your life like a ledger. Most of the entries are small. You find that they are enough.

choices.text: Read the ledger with kindness

effects.log: The small entries bend toward each other like grass. You do not tally. You simply read.

choices.text: Add one line to it, for tomorrow

effects.log: A promise, small and plain. You write it in the margin.

events.text: The thunder is still a long way off, and already the hair on your arms stands up. The storm is making its way to you like a guest who knows the address.

choices.text: Open the door and greet the thunder at the threshold

effects.log: You stand in the draught. The thunder, at last, is a presence with a warm edge.

choices.text: Prepare a seat for the guest

effects.log: A second cushion beside your own. The storm, you feel, appreciates the gesture.

choices.text: Pull the screens and let it come

effects.log: The room dims. You and the storm will meet unseen, as old combatants should.

events.text: You light a single lamp and set it in the window, to show the sky where you are. It seems the right manners for a visit of this size.

choices.text: Trim the wick so it burns clean

effects.log: A small act. The window glows steadily, and the sky, you feel, has noted it.

choices.text: Let the lamp gutter naturally

effects.log: It flickers, steadies, flickers. Your breath finds its rhythm.

events.text: Everything in you is ready and still you are not at ease, which you take to be the correct state. Someone with no fear would be in the wrong place.

choices.text: Take the fear as a sign of rightness and sit with it

effects.log: It shrinks to the size of a bird and perches on your shoulder. You are not alone.

choices.text: Walk the isle to wear the fear down

effects.log: Two circuits, and the legs steady first, then the heart.

choices.text: Share the fear with a friend by letter

effects.log: The reply comes at once: 'Me too. Good luck.' It is the best letter of your life.

events.text: While meditating you notice a sourness in your qi, like a thread of vinegar in the wine: small, old, and exactly where the foundation meets the floor.

choices.text: Follow the sourness to its root

effects.log: A tiny knot, tied long ago on a day of hurry. You trace the whole story.

choices.text: Rinse it with a week of plain breathing

effects.log: The sourness thins. It does not leave, but it is no longer the loudest voice.

events.text: A physician of the Nine Clouds reads your pulse for half an hour, then says: your left meridian was laid by someone in a hurry. It is you she means.

choices.text: Ask her to show you where the hurry was

effects.log: She points at a single hour of your youth. You nod, and feel it, and thank her.

choices.text: Dispute the diagnosis

effects.log: She smiles, and says to come back when you have finished arguing. You are back in a month.

events.text: You dig through your foundation as through the wall of a house, and find, behind the plaster, a gap you filled with whatever came to hand in a poorer century.

choices.text: Leave the gap, and note where it is

effects.log: Better to know the wall than to demolish it. You draw its outline.

choices.text: Chip out the old plaster

effects.log: A week of dust. Beneath is raw stone, honest, a little cold.

choices.text: Fill it with something better, slowly

effects.log: A paste of patience. It dries over a decade, and you check it nightly.

events.text: One of your old techniques has been drawing a hair too much from the golden core for all the time you have used it. The shortfall has become a lean.

choices.text: Restore the draw to its proper measure

effects.log: A tiny adjustment, repeated for months. The lean eases.

choices.text: Retire that technique for a season

effects.log: You miss it like a worn glove. The foundation breathes, level at last.

events.text: The mirror-pool shows your core as a lotus with one petal shorter than the rest. You have been breathing around it for so long that you thought it a feature.

choices.text: Study the short petal

effects.log: It is not damaged, only small. You decide to feed it first, and the rest after.

choices.text: Breathe into the petal until it matches

effects.log: Slow, dull work. A month, and the mirror shows a lotus nearly even.

choices.text: Love the lotus as it is

effects.log: Odd, and strangely healing. The petal stays short, and the flower no longer grieves.

events.text: A passing star-reader remarks, kindly, that you hold your breath at the top of every inhale. You do. You have since childhood, and so does your foundation.

choices.text: Exhale first, and then inhale

effects.log: The old catch is there. You ease it down a hair a week, for a year.

choices.text: Thank the star-reader and ask for more

effects.log: They have a dozen small notes more. The tea goes cold.

events.text: The flaw is not weakness exactly. It is a groove, worn by repetition, and the qi runs down it like water because that is what it knows.

choices.text: Re-cut the groove in a gentler line

effects.log: A patient year. The qi wanders at first, then finds the new channel and rests in it.

choices.text: Teach the water a second route, leave the first

effects.log: Two grooves. The old is the shorter, the new the wiser. You use both.

events.text: At this height flaws look small and are not. A hairline across the base of the foundation, and the whole tower of years above it leans.

choices.text: Trace the hairline with a finger of qi

effects.log: You feel its edge, thin as a thought. Marking it is already half the cure.

choices.text: Reinforce above it before you fix below

effects.log: Backwards, perhaps. The tower, at least, stops leaning for now.

choices.text: Rest the whole tower for a year

effects.log: You do nothing at all. The hairline, oddly, narrows.

events.text: You find an error older than your cultivation: a belief about what strength is. It sits in the foundation like a stone in a loaf, hard and unsuspected.

choices.text: Face the belief and ask whose it was

effects.log: It was a teacher's, long dead, and kind, and wrong. You forgive them.

choices.text: Chew around the stone

effects.log: Practical. You eat the loaf and carry the stone for later.

choices.text: Hold the stone up to a friend

effects.log: They weigh it, and laugh, and tell you of their own. Comfort in company.

events.text: A whisper of unevenness, deep in the foundation, that only an immortal of your standing could possibly feel, and that matters only because of your standing.

choices.text: Feel the unevenness without correcting it

effects.log: Your attention alone shifts it a hair. A strange, intimate fact.

choices.text: Straighten it in a single exhale

effects.log: A clean, risky motion. It nearly works. Next time, perhaps.

choices.text: Note it down for the next age

effects.log: A small slip in a drawer. Someone will thank you, or you will.

events.text: You decide to mend the flaw the slow way: a breath a day, aimed at the weak place, with no ambition above it. A pilgrim could do this. You are a pilgrim again.

choices.text: Keep the daily breath for a year

effects.log: A year of mornings at the weak place. You do not notice the day it heals.

choices.text: Let a bolder friend join you for a month

effects.log: They are impatient with your pace and fond of you anyway. You mend a little faster to spare them.

events.text: Your qi, patiently re-routed, finds the groove it should have taken all along. It is like watching a stream decide to go home.

choices.text: Follow the stream home

effects.log: You do not steer. The qi arrives and settles with a faint sigh.

choices.text: Dam the old groove with a small stone

effects.log: A simple blockage. The stream turns, and learns.

events.text: An old pill-master from the Nine Clouds lends you a remedy that tastes of rain on cold iron. It works while you sleep, and you wake with a straighter spine.

choices.text: Take the remedy exactly as directed

effects.log: Three nights, three bowls. You wake each morning straighter, and by the third you are tall.

choices.text: Ask the pill-master about the rain on iron

effects.log: She tells you of the tea-house on the third cloud where the water first fell. You go, and the water is better still.

events.text: For three seasons you turn your breath the other way. It feels like writing with the wrong hand. Then, one morning, it feels like your own.

choices.text: Hold the new breath-turn through the grey months

effects.log: Spring brings it. The wrong hand is the right hand now.

choices.text: Alternate the old and new, a week each

effects.log: It is clumsy and kind. By the end you can use either, and you favour neither.

choices.text: Teach the turn to a pupil to learn it better

effects.log: The pupil catches it in a week. Humbling, instructive.

events.text: The mending takes a decade of attention and a single afternoon of insight. You are never able to tell which was more of the work.

choices.text: Spend the afternoon of insight in a garden

effects.log: The decade bore the fruit. In the garden you only pick it.

choices.text: Credit the decade

effects.log: You raise a cup to the long steady days. They were the work.

events.text: You re-lay the foundation stone by stone, as a mason re-lays a wall, never all at once, always one course while the rest holds up the sky.

choices.text: Lay the next course slowly

effects.log: Each stone is a small decision. You are more careful than you were as a young builder.

choices.text: Check the old courses for cracks as you go

effects.log: Two hairlines, both mendable. The wall, you decide, will outlast you.

events.text: The mend closes without ceremony. Only the next time you reach for the gate, you notice it feels half a hand-span nearer than it did.

choices.text: Reach for the gate and feel the half-hand

effects.log: The gate is nearer. You do not press. You let the nearness be a quiet joy.

choices.text: Measure the distance and tell no one

effects.log: A private triumph. You smile at the cushion.

events.text: A rival you once resented provides the final piece, without knowing. A chance remark, and the shape of the mend becomes obvious. You send a fruit-basket.

choices.text: Send the fruit-basket with a real note

effects.log: The reply is warm and brief. The rivalry softens into a friendship of the gruff kind.

choices.text: Test the mend with the rival's remark in mind

effects.log: It fits like a key. You thank the rival silently every morning for a year.

events.text: The flaw mends the way a bone does: by being given time and rest and the exact pressure it needs, and by your not interfering.

choices.text: Let the mend be a slow bone

effects.log: You neither force nor ignore. Time does the main work.

choices.text: Give the mend its exact pressure, once a day

effects.log: A small dedicated ritual. Over seasons it turns into love of the work.

events.text: What was crooked is straight. What was thin has thickened. The foundation stands the way you meant it to, at last, and the quiet is deeper by a whole octave.

choices.text: Listen to the new octave

effects.log: A faint low note beneath all notes. You rest in it, tunefully.

choices.text: Praise the foundation aloud, as one praises a good house

effects.log: A silly gesture, and your eyes sting. It has earned the praise.

choices.text: Go on as if nothing happened

effects.log: Quiet, correct, a little shy. The quiet is now larger.

events.text: An immortal manual, bound in cloud-silk that tears if you read it angrily. You read it at first light, patient, one line to a cup of tea.

choices.text: Read slowly, as the silk asks

effects.log: A line, a sip, a pause. The silk stays whole, and so does your temper.

choices.text: Test one line at once, at the cushion

effects.log: It works, a little, in an unexpected corner of the body. You mark it.

events.text: The manual's author takes pains over small things: the angle of the tongue, the weight of the eyelids. You had thought those were for beginners.

choices.text: Practise the tongue angle for a week

effects.log: Dull, exact, strangely powerful. Your breath narrows to a clean thread.

choices.text: Practise the eyelid weight for a week

effects.log: The world quiets a shade. A small door opens in the forehead.

choices.text: Admit you skipped the basics and begin again

effects.log: Pride swallowed. The foundation thanks you in spring.

events.text: You copy a passage from the Scroll Hall of the Jade Court into your own notebook in your own hand, so that your hand may learn what your mind cannot yet say.

choices.text: Copy it out twice more

effects.log: By the third copy your hand knows the passage as a path knows a walker.

choices.text: Annotate the copy in the margin in your own words

effects.log: A dialogue with the author. In the third margin you disagree, and are right.

events.text: The method asks you to breathe as the sea of clouds breathes: out for a season, in for a season. You practise with a water-clock and much patience.

choices.text: Make the water-clock and keep the seasons

effects.log: A year at the pace of the sea. You wake slower and finer.

choices.text: Shorten the seasons to a week each

effects.log: A rough translation of the method. It still teaches, but it tires you.

choices.text: Ask a sailor of the clouds how they breathe

effects.log: They laugh, then show you. The sailor's way is easier than the scroll's.

events.text: Page after page of immortal method, and the thing you keep returning to is a margin note in a stranger's script, three words: 'Not yet. Wait.'

choices.text: Find the stranger who wrote the margin note

effects.log: A trail of three inked seals. At the end a retired archivist who remembers only the words.

choices.text: Do as the note says and wait

effects.log: The waiting is the page. A year later the next chapter reads like a door.

choices.text: Write beneath it: 'Waiting.'

effects.log: A modest reply, to a dead stranger. It feels like shaking a hand.

events.text: A cloud method ought to be taught person to person. You have only the scroll, so you read it aloud to an empty room and listen for where your voice stumbles.

choices.text: Read it to the empty room twice more

effects.log: The stumble moves. The second stumble is a lesson, the third is a joke.

choices.text: Read it to a visitor and have them stumble too

effects.log: You share where each of you balks. Between you the passage is complete.

events.text: At this height the manuals stop giving instructions and start giving questions. You collect them like pebbles and wonder which one is the key.

choices.text: Collect the questions in a jar

effects.log: A pebble each. By autumn the jar is heavy and the answers are rattling out.

choices.text: Answer one question a month, honestly

effects.log: Twelve answers a year. The first is a lie, the sixth is true.

events.text: The method describes the Dao as a river; the next page, as a stair; the next, as a silence. The author evidently could not decide, and you trust them more for it.

choices.text: Hold all three images and let them argue

effects.log: River, stair, silence. They settle on a shape you cannot name, and you stop trying.

choices.text: Write the author a courteous letter

effects.log: Of course it cannot be sent. Writing it clears the mind more than any answer.

choices.text: Choose the silence and practise it

effects.log: The simplest of the three. It is the hardest.

events.text: You study the method with the care of someone unwrapping a gift that may be a trap. Every phrase may be a door and every door may be a wall.

choices.text: Go through it line by line with a lamp

effects.log: Three traps found and disarmed, one door found and opened. It takes a season.

choices.text: Skip to the end and read it backwards

effects.log: Cheeky, and strangely it makes sense. The final line was always the first.

events.text: The oldest of the cloud methods you hold is written in a script no one living reads. You have learned it from the pictures, and the pictures have learned you.

choices.text: Learn a glyph a day from the pictures

effects.log: A year of glyphs. By winter you can read a sentence, and the sentence reads you.

choices.text: Copy the pictures and hang them up

effects.log: A wall of old pictures. Visitors stop and stare. Some stay.

choices.text: Put it aside until the pictures ask for you

effects.log: They do not ask. You pick it up anyway, a year later, with new eyes.

events.text: The manual's thirty-first page is gone. The stub is neat, as if cut with a ruler. Everything before it builds to a door and everything after assumes you have walked through.

choices.text: Fill the stub with a bookmark and read on

effects.log: The gap becomes a door you step over. You fall slightly, and catch yourself.

choices.text: Ask the stub what it remembers

effects.log: It remembers the scissors, you suppose. A bad joke. Still, you smile and sit up.

events.text: The Scroll Hall's copy and your own are identical, and both skip the same page. Someone wanted a gap. You begin to wonder who and why.

choices.text: Visit the Scroll Hall and ask whose hand cut it

effects.log: A keeper confesses it was always so. No one remembers why. The mystery is the point.

choices.text: Leave a note for the next reader beside the gap

effects.log: A tidy thing. You hope they find it before they lose heart.

choices.text: Reproduce the missing page from memory of the method

effects.log: It reads as confidently wrong. Strangely, it works for you.

events.text: You write to three libraries asking about the missing leaf. One reply comes in a month: a thin line of someone else's notes, in a slanting hand.

choices.text: Answer the slanting hand in a letter

effects.log: A correspondence of twelve letters. At the end you are practising a method that neither of you wrote.

choices.text: Keep the borrowed notes in the empty place

effects.log: They sit well. Some words from a stranger can hold up a page.

events.text: The gap in the text is exactly one page wide. You have laid a blank sheet in it, and every night you find yourself writing, then crossing out, a line.

choices.text: Write the line you cross out most often and stop crossing it out

effects.log: It is a plain sentence about patience. It does the work of a page.

choices.text: Leave the sheet blank on purpose

effects.log: You practise the blank. It teaches you to be without answers.

events.text: The scholar who first copied this manual left a note on the flyleaf: 'The missing page is the point.' You do not know whether to laugh or to weep.

choices.text: Laugh, and take the note as an instruction

effects.log: Laughing loosens the chest. You practise the point, the absence, for a season.

choices.text: Weep, briefly, for the scholar

effects.log: A stranger, long dead, who left you a gift of nothing. The tears are clean.

choices.text: Return the favour with a blank flyleaf in your own copy

effects.log: Yours will be another note, for the next. The chain goes on.

events.text: You reconstruct the lost page from the pages around it, as an astronomer finds an unseen star by the wobble of its neighbours. What you derive is strange.

choices.text: Trust your reconstruction and practise it

effects.log: It feels foreign and just. The foreignness fades over a month.

choices.text: Test it against the neighbour pages in turn

effects.log: A wobble remains. You adjust. The star is nearly found.

events.text: An old immortal tells you over tea that the page was removed deliberately, centuries ago, because it works on the reader the way a mirror works on a vain man.

choices.text: Ask what the mirror showed the vain man

effects.log: A long story, and a dark one. The old immortal ends it with a laugh. 'Look at it anyway.'

choices.text: Look in the mirror-pool and be honest

effects.log: You see a tired face with good eyes. It will do.

choices.text: Leave the page missing and thank the one who cut it

effects.log: You say it to the empty room. The room, in its way, accepts.

events.text: The missing page is the one on which the method becomes your own. Every reader writes it differently. Yours, you now see, has been taking shape for years.

choices.text: Write the page in your own hand tonight

effects.log: It runs to a sentence and a half. It is the truest thing you have written.

choices.text: Wait for the page to finish writing itself

effects.log: It does, somewhere in a dream. You wake and set it down.

events.text: You find the page at last in a trunk of unrelated accounts, folded small. It is blank except for one line: 'You already know.'

choices.text: Hold the blank page to the lamp

effects.log: The sentence stays. You take it as a gift and a rebuke.

choices.text: Live as though you already knew

effects.log: Next morning you sit differently. The method takes your word for it.

events.text: Without the page, the method grew a slow arc in you of its own. When a copy of the page finally reaches you, it matches what you have already, in fact, become.

choices.text: Compare the arrived page with your own

effects.log: They differ in three words. You decide whose are better, then decide not to say.

choices.text: Frame them together, side by side

effects.log: A pair on the wall. Visitors guess which is the original, and always get it wrong.

choices.text: Burn the arrived page respectfully

effects.log: It had said what it should. You need nothing more from it.

events.text: The cloud method wants you to sink your qi down; the art you learned in your youth wants it to rise. Your golden core has been complaining for a month.

choices.text: Let the golden core speak

effects.log: Rise, sink. The golden core chooses sink, with an apologetic sigh toward the old art.

choices.text: Hold the qi in the middle and breathe it both ways

effects.log: A sloshing, fair arrangement. The complaint subsides into an ache.

events.text: Your old palm form, trained through three thousand rainy mornings, answers the cloud method's first movement with its own. The two meet in your forearm like arguing cousins.

choices.text: Let the forearm settle it

effects.log: The palm yields, and the method yields back. They end in a draw.

choices.text: Practise the palm form in the cloud method's rhythm

effects.log: Strange and slow, and it feels like your native tongue spoken in a new accent.

choices.text: Put the old palm away for a month

effects.log: You miss it at the third dawn. Absence makes the hand clearer.

events.text: The cloud method teaches you to yield, and your oldest sword form was built entirely out of not yielding. Half of you wants to bow, and half to cut.

choices.text: Draw the old sword once, at dawn, in honour

effects.log: No yielding. The cut is clean. You sheathe it with a bow to the pupil you were.

choices.text: Learn to yield with the sword drawn

effects.log: A strange discipline: sharp, and soft. It takes seasons.

choices.text: Bow, and leave the cutting to the young

effects.log: A kind of wisdom, a kind of surrender. You feel lighter and a little hollow.

events.text: You catch your hands falling into the old stance by themselves. It is a good stance. It is also wrong for this air, which is thin on the ground and thick overhead.

choices.text: Let the hands finish the stance, then step out of it

effects.log: A moment of the old and a step into the new. It teaches your feet a frontier.

choices.text: Turn the stance upward, toward the open air

effects.log: It is the old stance reaching for a new sky. It works shyly.

events.text: A younger immortal laughs, not unkindly, when you demonstrate a mortal foundation form. 'We stopped doing that,' they say. 'It still works,' you say, and it does, a little.

choices.text: Show them the form again, slowly

effects.log: They watch, then try. Their version has three flaws and one genius.

choices.text: Accept the laugh and move on

effects.log: A warm little shrug. The form stays in your bones.

choices.text: Ask them what they do instead

effects.log: They show a gesture of pure cloud. It is lovely, and not what you need, but you bow.

events.text: The cloud method and the old art disagree about where the centre is. You have spent a century wondering whether to arbitrate or to let them fight it out.

choices.text: Arbitrate: give the centre a day to each

effects.log: A dull court, a quiet verdict. Both arts accept it.

choices.text: Let them fight it out for a season

effects.log: They bruise each other, and you. At the end the centre has moved to where you are.

events.text: Your old art taught you to guard your gates. The cloud method asks you to leave them open. Your fingers curl in your sleep, trained by a century of guarding.

choices.text: Open the gates and let the old art stand watch

effects.log: Open, and watched. A strange pairing that settles into peace.

choices.text: Uncurl your fingers in sleep with a night-ritual

effects.log: Each night you flex them gently. After a year they uncurl on their own.

events.text: The old art is not wrong. It is a language, and the cloud method is a different language, and you are caught translating between them with every breath.

choices.text: Learn to translate aloud

effects.log: You mumble each breath in two tongues. A comedy, and a truth.

choices.text: Stop translating and let the two meet in the middle

effects.log: In the middle there is no language, only breath. You stay there.

choices.text: Pick one tongue for a century

effects.log: A hard choice, honestly made. You are the plainer for it, and calmer.

events.text: You discover the two methods have the same bones under different skin. The old forms were the cloud method's grandparents, wearing a mortal's coat.

choices.text: Honour the old art as a grandparent

effects.log: You bow to it before each session. It pays you back in quiet.

choices.text: Peel the coat off the old forms

effects.log: Under it, the forms are exactly the cloud method's own. You see the family face.

events.text: At the last, the old art and the new fall away from each other like two hands unclasping, and what is left in the palm is neither: just the clear fact of your own motion.

choices.text: Rest in the empty palm

effects.log: There is nothing in it, and everything. You stay a while.

choices.text: Name the motion

effects.log: A silly name, a private one. It makes it easier to carry.

choices.text: Teach the motion to no one

effects.log: A private art, held lightly. It will outlast you in a form no one can copy.

events.text: You go down to the edge of the isle and watch the Sea of Clouds roll under you in long, slow, silvery swells. A cormorant of the clouds rides one and does not look up.

choices.text: Follow the cormorant with your eyes to the horizon

effects.log: It rides and dips and is gone. The distance holds the shape of its going.

choices.text: Sit on the rim and breathe with the swell

effects.log: Long in, long out, in step with a thing a hundred miles wide.

events.text: The sea is low this morning and the isle peaks stand out like the backs of sleeping whales. You could almost walk from shoulder to shoulder to the far horizon.

choices.text: Walk the peaks in imagination, whale to whale

effects.log: A long mental stride. You wake with your legs aching and your mind wide.

choices.text: Step off the edge onto the sea

effects.log: Of course you fall, a short way, onto a drifting bank. A thrill and a lesson.

choices.text: Name the whales

effects.log: Old Mossback, Saltlip, Little Uncle. The sea, delighted, returns the courtesy in birdsong.

events.text: A tide of cloud comes up the cliff face at dawn and fills the valley in a quarter-hour. It goes out as softly. You realise it is the sea's way of breathing.

choices.text: Watch it come all the way up and fill the valley

effects.log: It breathes in. You breathe in. It is a long, wet, perfect minute.

choices.text: Go down into the cloud as it rises

effects.log: Grey and cool and silent. You lose the path and find the quiet.

events.text: Standing in the Sea of Clouds up to your chest, you feel qi moving in it, an immense drift of intention with no hurry in it at all. You match your breath and are carried.

choices.text: Match the drift, then loosen it

effects.log: The qi follows the intention, with no hurry, no edge. You let it drift you home.

choices.text: Stand there until you feel the sea's age

effects.log: It is older than the isle and gentler than the wind. It calls you young, and means it.

events.text: The sea is full of memory. Some days it shows you images at the bottom of the swell: a roof-tile, a river-boat, a child's red cap. They are other people's lives, drifting past.

choices.text: Catch the red cap in the swell

effects.log: It dissolves in your hands. Yet you remember a small child's laugh.

choices.text: Look away, respecting the privacy of strangers

effects.log: A courtesy to unseen lives. The sea turns its pictures to the wall.

choices.text: Ask the sea to show a life you have forgotten

effects.log: A slow pour of grey. Then a doorway you once stepped through. You step through it again.

events.text: The Sea of Clouds does not argue. It rises where it is let rise and falls where it must fall. You study its manners and apply them to your meridians.

choices.text: Rise without argument

effects.log: You rise where you are let, fall where you must. The meridians smooth.

choices.text: Try the sea's manners for a day

effects.log: No pushing, no pulling. By night the bruises you did not know you had are gone.

events.text: At dusk the sea goes bronze, then rose, then blue-black. Tonight it holds still so long that you begin to think your own stillness is the thing that is moving.

choices.text: Wait for the blue-black

effects.log: It comes, and it holds, and you with it. The moving stillness is yours.

choices.text: Walk back at the bronze and cook supper

effects.log: Sensible and warm. The sea keeps its own counsel.

events.text: The Sea of Clouds is thicker today, almost solid. A flock of wild geese flies over, and for a moment you see their shadows on the sea, a thousand miles below.

choices.text: Lean out and watch the geese-shadows

effects.log: A thousand miles of grey and a line of small black grace. You carry it home.

choices.text: Ride a thick bank for a mile

effects.log: Wobbling, and thrilling. You return pink-cheeked and grinning.

events.text: You lie on your back on the very edge and let the sea hold the isle. The isle holds you. A long, large quiet falls over everything and you rest inside it.

choices.text: Let the sea hold the isle a bit longer

effects.log: Another hour. The isle sighs. The sea sighs back.

choices.text: Sing something small into the quiet

effects.log: The quiet takes it and gives it back sweeter. You rest in the echo.

events.text: At this height the Sea of Clouds is no longer below but all around, a bright mist without a horizon. You walk in it and your footprints close behind you, one by one, like questions answered.

choices.text: Walk until the footprints stop closing

effects.log: They do, eventually, in a little line of questions that are not answered. You keep the line.

choices.text: Stand and let the mist have you

effects.log: The edge dissolves. You are the mist, a little, and the mist is a little you.

choices.text: Turn and watch the footprints close

effects.log: One by one, patient, kind. A good lesson in how little is kept.

events.text: On the night of the star tide the sky leans down. Every star seems a hand's breadth nearer, and the qi in the air is thick enough to drink.

choices.text: Open your mouth like a child and breathe

effects.log: The air is thick and sweet. A giddiness, a lightness, a thousand tiny winks.

choices.text: Sit in the clear dark and let the tide pass over

effects.log: It passes. You are a shore, and the shore is glad.

events.text: The Star Sea Pavilion's seers have announced the tide with their gongs. You climb to the rim of the isle and open your mouth like a child to snow.

choices.text: Climb to the rim and wait for the gong

effects.log: The gong comes. The tide rises. You feel like a drum.

choices.text: Wait on the lower terrace, away from the show

effects.log: Quiet, just you and the sky. The tide is gentler on the lower slope.

choices.text: Bring a cup and let it fill with starlight

effects.log: The cup, at dawn, holds a faint cool shimmer. You drink, and your eyes are bright for a week.

events.text: When the star tide runs, the heavens pour a long cool glimmer into the meridians of anyone who sits still enough. You sit, and the glimmer is a river.

choices.text: Let the glimmer run on its own

effects.log: A river, indeed. It finds its bed in your meridians and rests there.

choices.text: Direct the glimmer to the weakest place

effects.log: Like a gardener, you water the dry corners. The tide is generous.

events.text: A star falls slowly, as they do at the tide, drawing a line of light you can follow with your eyes. You follow it into your own golden core and it dissolves there.

choices.text: Follow the line down into the golden core

effects.log: It dissolves with a faint chime. Your core is, for a night, a little brighter.

choices.text: Let the line pass and watch the next

effects.log: A procession of lights. You note them, and wish them well.

events.text: The tide is lower than it was in your youth, or you are higher. Either way the stars feel nearer, more crowded, all murmuring at once in an old family dialect.

choices.text: Greet the murmuring in the old dialect

effects.log: A few words come back. The stars, delighted, murmur louder.

choices.text: Listen without trying to translate

effects.log: Stars speaking at once make a hush, not a din. You rest in it.

choices.text: Admit that you are the one who climbed

effects.log: A small, wry honesty. The sky has no opinion, but the evening feels fair.

events.text: You were taught that the star tide fortifies the bones. That is true, and the sages tell only half: it also forgives the day before.

choices.text: Test the day-before's forgiveness

effects.log: A small grudge you carried slides away. You will remember it tomorrow, but lighter.

choices.text: Fortify the bones deliberately

effects.log: A tingle in the long ones. By morning you feel like a taller tree.

events.text: On this tide your qi quivers with the swell. You hold it as one holds a full cup walking across a bright room, mindful and unhurried and quite happy.

choices.text: Walk the bright room with the full cup

effects.log: Slow, gentle, mindful, quite happy. Nothing spills.

choices.text: Let a little spill, on purpose

effects.log: A drop on the floor. A small, bright puddle. The room is better for it.

events.text: The tide brings, beneath its glow, a low thrum like a bell rung in another world. Your bones answer it. For a moment you are tuned to the entire sky.

choices.text: Answer the bell with your bones

effects.log: A deep hum under the skin. For a breath you are one string among a billion.

choices.text: Hum a low note back

effects.log: The note carries. Somewhere beyond the isles, perhaps, a listener hears.

events.text: Seven bright stars cross the isle in procession and you recognise, with a small start, the posture of an old teacher you once saluted from below.

choices.text: Greet the procession by bowing

effects.log: The stars do not break stride, but the last one dips, perhaps. You smile.

choices.text: Recall the teacher and speak to the posture

effects.log: A few warm words. The memory warms, and the sky seems to listen.

choices.text: Take the posture yourself and hold it

effects.log: Seven stars, and you, in a line. A pleasant straight ache follows.

events.text: The tide at this height stops being a thing that happens to you and becomes a thing you happen to be part of. The stars do not pour; they simply include you.

choices.text: Include the stars in return

effects.log: You open your meridians to being one more bright thing. They fit.

choices.text: Sit as a part of the tide and ask nothing

effects.log: No gain, no loss. The tide includes you and goes on.

choices.text: Mark the hour and go to bed

effects.log: Sometimes the right thing is sleep. The tide will be back.

events.text: The wind at your isle comes from nowhere in particular and goes the same way. You have sat in it for so many years that you can tell its mood by its smell.

choices.text: Read the smell of the wind this morning

effects.log: Cold stone, pine, a faint sweetness from the lower isles. A day of mild temper.

choices.text: Sit out in it with your eyes closed

effects.log: A long hour in the mood of the wind. Your qi picks up its habits.

events.text: A hard wind rises in the afternoon and tears the paper from your window. You let it. The wind is not hostile, only enormous, and has other business.

choices.text: Mend the window paper and thank the wind

effects.log: The new paper holds for a day. The wind approves, in its way.

choices.text: Leave the window open and the paper gone

effects.log: A bare frame, a free sky. The wind sorts your papers kindly into piles.

choices.text: Try to catch the paper in your qi

effects.log: It slips, loops, flutters back. You laugh, and catch it the third time.

events.text: You watch a single leaf cross the whole valley on the wind, turning and dipping, never once resisting. You attempt the same with your qi and fail, and fail more gracefully.

choices.text: Practise being the leaf

effects.log: You fail, softly. The failing is a kind of flying.

choices.text: Follow the leaf across the valley in your mind

effects.log: A long, calm journey. You land with it in a field of white clover.

events.text: At the top of the morning there is a wind that comes from the east, the way a wise thought does: unannounced, clean, and gone before you quite hold it.

choices.text: Say good morning to the east wind

effects.log: It brushes your cheek, once. A greeting, a blessing.

choices.text: Hold the wise thought before it flees

effects.log: It stays a moment, and says three words. You do not repeat them.

events.text: The wind carries the sound of distant temple bells from three isles at once, and for a moment you hear them as a single chord, resolved.

choices.text: Hear the chord and resolve with it

effects.log: Three bells, one note. You hum the fourth, and the sky nods.

choices.text: Name the three temples

effects.log: Cloud-Gate, Little Reed, Stillwater. A tidy map of the sounds.

events.text: In the wind you notice a gap, a pocket of stillness moving through the gale. You step into it. It carries you for a hundred paces, then lets you go.

choices.text: Step into the pocket and ride

effects.log: A hundred paces of pure ease. You step out light and ready.

choices.text: Study the pocket and map its moving edge

effects.log: A drifting calm in the gale. You note its size and speed.

events.text: The old immortals say that the wind is the sky thinking out loud. Today it is thinking about autumn, and about you, rather fondly.

choices.text: Listen to the autumn thought

effects.log: A grey, golden, thinning thought. It is about you, and kind.

choices.text: Answer the wind's thought with your own

effects.log: Quietly, from the doorway. The wind listens with its whole body.

events.text: A storm wind crosses the isle and every window rattles. You find yourself unafraid, even glad, as if an old general had marched through and saluted you.

choices.text: Salute the general

effects.log: A small bow, a straightening of the back. The wind rattles the windows once more, and departs.

choices.text: Stand in the doorway and take the gale

effects.log: It buffets you. You are a post in a river. Both of you are fine.

events.text: You hang a thread from the eaves and watch it all day. Where it bends, there is something to learn. Where it hangs straight, there is more.

choices.text: Watch the thread where it hangs straight

effects.log: The straight places are the quiet ones. You note them.

choices.text: Learn from where it bends

effects.log: A map of the air in a single bent thread. You draw it.

choices.text: Cut the thread and let it fly

effects.log: A small release. The thread sails away on its own business.

events.text: At the height of the Upper Realm the wind is hardly weather any more. It is a language, and every gust a word, and you almost, almost have the grammar.

choices.text: Practise one gust of the grammar

effects.log: A single word of wind. It sounds like an exhale, and means: enough.

choices.text: Let the grammar stay unlearned

effects.log: A bright, friendly mystery. The wind seems to prefer it.

choices.text: Speak back in the wind's own tongue, badly

effects.log: It laughs and corrects you. You are an apprentice again, and delighted.

events.text: You climb the White Stairs for a few hundred steps, as you do on good days. Each step is polished by a million feet and warm as skin from the sun.

choices.text: Climb to the three-hundredth and rest

effects.log: Warm stone, warm hands. You sit, and the sun-heat travels up your spine.

choices.text: Touch each step as you pass

effects.log: A little bow of the fingers. By the end you know the stair like a friend.

events.text: Halfway up the White Stairs there is a landing with a stone bench. Today a young immortal sits on it, panting, and you sit beside them without a word.

choices.text: Share the bench and your flask

effects.log: You say little. They say less. It is enough.

choices.text: Tell them the secret of the landing

effects.log: That everyone rests here, once. They laugh, and rise taller.

choices.text: Leave them the bench and climb on

effects.log: A gentle courtesy. You hear them following by the second turn.

events.text: The White Stairs hold a memory in every tread. Today, on the hundredth step, you recall something said in the mortal village long ago, and your eyes sting.

choices.text: Let the memory come all the way up

effects.log: A voice, a lamp, a meal. You sit with it until the stone cools.

choices.text: Whisper a name into the tread

effects.log: The step is warm under your palm. It keeps the name.

events.text: You go down the White Stairs, which no one does. It is slow, and the mortals' faint dust rises to meet you. You find that dust curiously fine.

choices.text: Walk down among the dust

effects.log: It is fine as flour. The mortal world rises gently, and you taste it.

choices.text: Turn and climb back up with a pinch of it

effects.log: Mortal dust in your pocket. A small, odd, precious thing.

events.text: On the stairs, a petitioner kneels with a letter, and a guard of the Celestial Ministries bars them. You pass, and the guard lowers its eyes, and the petitioner does not rise.

choices.text: Stop and help the petitioner to read the letter

effects.log: The guard turns his back. The petitioner stands, and walks on, with a path.

choices.text: Speak to the guard and ask for a hearing

effects.log: A courtesy among officials. The letter is accepted, slowly.

choices.text: Pass on, and carry the sight

effects.log: You do not forget the kneeling. A small hard stone in the shoe, for later.

events.text: The stairs are empty before dawn, and every step rings under your sandal like a struck bowl. You climb in time with the ringing and do not tire.

choices.text: Climb in time with the ringing

effects.log: A drum made of steps. By the top you have forgotten your own weight.

choices.text: Sit at the bottom and listen to it ring away

effects.log: A long bowl-sound that thins into the dawn. You rest in the afterglow.

events.text: You have climbed the White Stairs so many times that your feet know the chips and hollows. They teach you something about the long journey of a single foot.

choices.text: Learn the hollows by heart

effects.log: A map in the soles. Each hollow is a century of some stranger's heel.

choices.text: Fill one hollow with a pinch of white sand

effects.log: A small repair. The stair, in its way, notices.

events.text: A thin cloud has come down onto the White Stairs, and you climb through it as through a veil. At the next landing you are a younger self, for a breath.

choices.text: Climb through to the younger self

effects.log: You wave. They do not see you, and then they do. Brief, bright, confusing.

choices.text: Wait for the cloud to pass

effects.log: It does. The younger self goes with it. You climb on, warmer.

events.text: The topmost tread of the White Stairs lies in the open sky. Today you stand on it and look down at every step you have taken, each a little white tooth of years.

choices.text: Count the teeth of years

effects.log: They are many and each is bright. You stop counting at the four-thousandth.

choices.text: Bow to the stair

effects.log: A small, odd gesture. A cool wind wraps your shoulders for a moment.

choices.text: Sit on the highest tread and eat your supper

effects.log: Rice and pickle, in the open sky. A good, ordinary meal.

events.text: The stairs, at your height, are no longer a way up but a way of remembering the climb. You sit on the lowest tread and feel the whole stair above you, a long spine of effort.

choices.text: Feel the whole stair above you

effects.log: A spine of effort, humming faintly. You lie against it and rest.

choices.text: Rise and climb one step, just one

effects.log: A tiny act, enough. The stair, at last, is a thing you walk.

events.text: An old teacher's words come back to you out of nowhere, as clear as if spoken yesterday: 'Do not hurry the thing that is already on its way.'

choices.text: Rest in the thing already on its way

effects.log: Hurry subsides. A slow wave is coming, and you sit up to meet it.

choices.text: Say the teacher's line aloud

effects.log: It sounds smaller and truer aloud. You smile, a little wet-eyed.

events.text: A rival sneers across the courtyard that you are slow. You are. The remark is a good deal truer than they meant, and you thank them privately for it.

choices.text: Admit to the rival that they were right

effects.log: A tiny, ruinous honesty. They are speechless, then gracious.

choices.text: Keep your slowness and be proud of it

effects.log: A modest pride. The rival's sneer finds nothing to bite.

choices.text: Quicken one thing, as an experiment

effects.log: A small speed in a single practice. It helps, and it hurts a little.

events.text: At the tea-house on the Jade Court's lower terrace you overhear a Star Reader tell an apprentice: 'It is not the gate that is closed. It is the hand that is clenched.'

choices.text: Unclench the hand a finger at a time

effects.log: The thumb is the worst. When it opens, the gate feels half a hand-span closer.

choices.text: Ask the Star Reader what they meant

effects.log: They smile and say the apprentice can answer. The apprentice cannot. You laugh.

events.text: A fellow immortal, passing, says only: 'You look like you are carrying it.' You do not ask what they mean. You put it down.

choices.text: Put it down: whatever it is

effects.log: You set down an invisible bundle on the stair. The step beneath feels pleased.

choices.text: Ask them what it was

effects.log: They are gone. You sit with the not-knowing, a patient guest.

events.text: The old keeper at the Scroll Hall says, apropos of nothing, that the best readers are those who need the book least. You mull it for a decade.

choices.text: Turn the line on yourself, gently

effects.log: You need the book less than you thought. You also need it more. A paradox you enjoy.

choices.text: Thank the keeper with a pot of tea

effects.log: A shy smile. The keeper adds a note to your records, and a bun.

events.text: A rival's last words to you on the cloud-court were: 'Enough of my doing it for you.' You did not understand. You do, now.

choices.text: Do one thing today without being carried

effects.log: A small effort, clumsy. The sky does not mind, and you do not either.

choices.text: Find the rival and thank them

effects.log: Very late, and very warm. They tell you they knew.

events.text: At a banquet, an immortal you hardly know raises a cup and murmurs: 'To the long way round.' It is the only toast you remember from the whole century.

choices.text: Return the toast with the same cup

effects.log: To the long way round. You drink, and so does the unknown immortal, a hundred miles apart.

choices.text: Take the long way home that night

effects.log: A longer road, a better evening. You see three things you had never seen.

events.text: Someone in the crowd at the Court calls you by a title you gave up long ago, and for a moment you are very young and very certain, and the certainty is a useful ghost.

choices.text: Wear the old title for a day

effects.log: It fits like an old coat, a little tight. You are again the one who was sure.

choices.text: Gently correct the caller

effects.log: A smile and a name. The caller, startled, bows deeper.

choices.text: Let the ghost walk beside you

effects.log: A tall, loud presence, a bit foolish. You find you are fond of it.

events.text: A rival leaves a note on your door: 'You were right.' Nothing else. It has more weight than a stack of treatises, and you keep it in your sleeve.

choices.text: Reply with a note of your own

effects.log: Two words: 'Thank you.' They are enough, as the first two were.

choices.text: Read the note until the folds soften

effects.log: The paper grows soft as cloth. You keep it for an age.

choices.text: Tell no one, and be glad

effects.log: A secret kindness, held lightly.

events.text: A newcomer, awed, asks you one honest question about the gate, and your answer surprises you both. You had not known you knew it until you heard it said.

choices.text: Teach them what you did not know you knew

effects.log: It comes out in a plain, patient run. They write it on their sleeve.

choices.text: Thank them for asking

effects.log: A simple courtesy, long overdue in the world. They glow.

events.text: The Jade Void Sect teaches that a sword is a sentence. At their white terraces you study how a single line of jade steel can say more than a library, and say it politely.

choices.text: Spend a week learning the sword's grammar

effects.log: Subject, stroke, silence. You write one clean sentence in jade steel and burn the draft.

choices.text: Ask why the terraces float over nothing

effects.log: A senior smiles: 'So that no one builds under them.' You laugh, and feel the point.

choices.text: Watch the morning drill from the rail

effects.log: Four hundred swords, one breath. You take the breath and leave the swords.

events.text: The Nine Clouds Palace keeps its alchemists humble by making them tend fires for a decade before they may open a furnace. You spend a month at the bellows, and learn.

choices.text: Take the bellows for a month

effects.log: Sweat, ash, rhythm. The fire teaches you to listen with your palms.

choices.text: Stoke only, and do not ask for the furnace

effects.log: Humility is the door here. A steward notices, and nods.

events.text: The Star Sea Pavilion trains by reading: charts, tides, faces. Their way of cultivating is to notice. You sit with their seers and notice, for once, how much you miss.

choices.text: Learn to read a tide-table of faces

effects.log: The seers teach you the first signs. You see boredom everywhere after.

choices.text: Notice your own missing details at dinner

effects.log: The seat on your left was empty, and you had not seen. A good, humbling lesson.

choices.text: Sell them a small true thing for a small true thing

effects.log: A fair trade, quietly kept. The Pavilion remembers fair traders.

events.text: The Celestial Ministries cultivate by rule: each hour for one thing, each thing in its hour. It seems stifling until the twelfth day, when it becomes a kind of freedom.

choices.text: Follow the hours for twelve days

effects.log: On the twelfth, the rule dissolves into ease. You bow to a clock for the first time.

choices.text: Keep only the rule of the first hour

effects.log: A single anchor in the day. It is enough to lean on.

choices.text: Ask a Minister who wrote the hours

effects.log: 'A very tired person,' she says, 'who wanted to rest.' You see the kindness in the grid.

events.text: In the Demon Realm they say strength is the only law, and they cultivate openly, with hunger. You watch, disquieted to find that you admire the honesty.

choices.text: Watch the demons train in the pit

effects.log: Honest, ferocious, joyful. You leave a little ashamed of your restraint.

choices.text: Say plainly what you admire

effects.log: They are startled, and pleased. A demon captain offers a drink, and you accept.

choices.text: Leave before the hunger takes you too

effects.log: A careful retreat. You carry the pit's heat home in your cheeks.

events.text: An archivist of the Jade Void explains that her sect's cultivation is an unlearning: strip the blade of everything but the cut. You try it with your breath.

choices.text: Strip your breath to the cut

effects.log: No flourish, no sigh, just the clean line of air. Dull for a day, bright for a month.

choices.text: Ask the archivist what she unlearned first

effects.log: 'My name for it,' she says. You spend the evening without names.

events.text: The Nine Clouds hold that every furnace is a small cosmos, and cultivation is the art of keeping it in balance. You come away with a new respect for gentle heat.

choices.text: Keep a furnace of your own for a season

effects.log: A small one, tended with respect. It teaches you the weight of gentle heat.

choices.text: Study how the Palace balances nine fires

effects.log: A diagram of nine clouds and nine tempers. You copy it and wonder which one is yours.

events.text: The Star Sea's way is to ask what the sky already wants and then be there. It is not so different from asking what you want, and both are hard.

choices.text: Ask the sky what it wants and wait

effects.log: Nothing, at first. Then something very specific about breakfast. You laugh.

choices.text: Ask yourself the same question and compare

effects.log: The two answers are close. The gap between them is the work.

events.text: A Celestial Minister tells you that cultivation is simply the law of oneself obeyed. You nod, and later realise how rarely you have obeyed yours.

choices.text: Obey your own law for a day

effects.log: It turns out to be strict and tender. You are tired and glad by evening.

choices.text: Write down the laws you have broken

effects.log: Eleven small ones. You mend three, and note the rest for tomorrow.

choices.text: Thank the Minister and say nothing more

effects.log: A compliment of silence. She inclines her head, a degree.

events.text: At the Demon Realm's pit of thunder an old demon laughs at you for being sad. 'We cultivate by wanting,' it says. 'You cultivate by wanting not to want. Who is the greater glutton?'

choices.text: Admit you are the greater glutton

effects.log: The demon roars with laughter and pours you a bowl. You drink to the pit and to yourself.

choices.text: Answer that wanting not to want is also hunger

effects.log: Silence. Then a grudging nod. You have been understood by an old enemy.

choices.text: Leave without answering, and think it over for a century

effects.log: A long, slow rumination. It pays off in surprising ways.

events.text: A spirit stone sits in each of the four corners of your gathering array. Their glow is the colour of old milk, and the qi they release smells faintly of rain on slate.

choices.text: Check each corner stone's glow

effects.log: Four steady glows, one a shade paler. You swap it with the east one for balance.

choices.text: Sit in the milk-white light and breathe the slate rain

effects.log: A scent of old rooms after storms. The qi comes quiet and even.

events.text: You set a Low-grade stone in the array's socket and feel the draw begin, a thread of qi no thicker than a hair, steady as a heartbeat.

choices.text: Feed the thread slowly for a season

effects.log: Hair-thin, and exact. The thread thickens by a hair, too, and you are content.

choices.text: Leave the socket empty for a night to feel the difference

effects.log: The room without it is bare, and you with it are bare. You set the stone back reverently.

events.text: The stones in your array have been in place for a century. One has gone grey and lost its glow, like a coal. You replace it with a ceremony of your own.

choices.text: Hold a small funeral for the grey stone

effects.log: A cup of tea, a bow. It has done its work and goes to rest in a jar.

choices.text: Recharge it in the star tide instead

effects.log: A patient, graceful dawn. It glows faintly, as a coal remembers.

events.text: You pour the last of a Mid-grade stone into your breath and the array dims. A moment's hush, then you set a fresh one, and the room fills like a bowl.

choices.text: Wait through the hush

effects.log: The room is an empty bowl for a moment, and then, filling, it feels deeper than before.

choices.text: Set the fresh stone with both hands

effects.log: A small ceremony. The array answers with a slightly warmer hum.

events.text: The array hums at a pitch that matches your resting pulse. Spirit stones are only the tinder. The hum is the fire, and the fire is the habit of sitting.

choices.text: Hum along with the array

effects.log: The room hums. A visitor at the door hesitates, then leans on the lintel to listen.

choices.text: Sit without the stones and let the habit carry you

effects.log: You can. It is slower. You are surprised how much of the array was you.

events.text: A High-grade stone, rare and heavy, lies on your palm like a small moon. You hold it a while before you use it, out of a kind of respect.

choices.text: Hold the moon until it warms

effects.log: It takes an hour. It warms like a cheek, and gives you a little of its light.

choices.text: Return it unused to the vault

effects.log: A restraint, strange to some. The vault-keeper nods, as if he expected it.

choices.text: Share a thin shaving with the lower isles

effects.log: A speck, ground to dust, scattered on dry herb-beds. In spring they bloom like jewels.

events.text: The array's pattern is older than you and was drawn by a steadier hand. You trace it with a finger each month, and each month it teaches you again to be exact.

choices.text: Trace a new line parallel to the old

effects.log: The two lines hum a third note. You stop at once and rub the second out, carefully.

choices.text: Trace only the original and learn its hand

effects.log: A steadier hand than yours, long dead. For an hour yours is as steady.

events.text: You test the array by lifting a single stone from it. The pattern gasps, then rebalances. You put the stone back, a little shaken at how much was held by how little.

choices.text: Run the test again to feel the rebalance

effects.log: The pattern gasps and sighs. You learn a lot about how a house of qi holds together.

choices.text: Leave the stone out for a night

effects.log: The array hums sadly, then bravely. By morning you have a deeper respect.

events.text: A thin line of frost runs across a Supreme-grade stone lent to you for a ritual. It is the cold of a very large, very deep place, and your qi shivers in welcome.

choices.text: Press your palm to the frost

effects.log: Cold, vast, and wise. Your qi shivers in welcome and learns the size of the deep.

choices.text: Return the stone with thanks and a clean cloth

effects.log: The lender is moved. A gentle reputation spreads.

choices.text: Draw the frost into a ritual phrase

effects.log: A few lines to carry the cold into other nights. It works, faintly.

events.text: At the last, the array does not pull from the stones at all. They sit in their sockets, gleaming, and the qi simply rises around you out of habit, as water does in a well.

choices.text: Sit as the water rises in the well

effects.log: It rises. You sink into it and are carried.

choices.text: Gather the stones and give them away

effects.log: Light hands, light heart. The qi still rises, from the habit alone.

choices.text: Polish them for the joy of it

effects.log: Four stones, one cloth. They shine like old friends.

events.text: You are sitting in the doorway at dusk when the Dao brushes past like a cat. For one breath you glimpse its tail, and every thought stops.

choices.text: Hold still, so the cat may return

effects.log: It does not. But the doorway is warmer than it was, and you sit in the warmth.

choices.text: Describe the tail to yourself, quickly
