effects.log: Three words, then more. The tail was longer than you thought.

events.text: The comprehension comes the way you step off a stair that is not there. A small lurch, a sudden lightness, and the old dark floor of your understanding is a ceiling.

choices.text: Stand on the ceiling a while

effects.log: A fine unnatural vantage. Every old thought looks different from above.

choices.text: Step back down carefully and rest

effects.log: The lurch fades. A calm grows where the stair was not.

events.text: You see, in an ordinary leaf falling, the entire structure of the thing you have been studying for centuries. It lasts as long as the leaf takes to land.

choices.text: Follow the leaf to the ground

effects.log: It lands. The structure sinks in with it, and you hold the shape until supper.

choices.text: Pick up the leaf and keep it in a book

effects.log: A small, bright keepsake. Years later it still hums, faintly.

events.text: A flash of the Dao arrives in a dream, disguised as a village market. You wake and cannot say what happened, only that you are changed by a small, specific amount.

choices.text: Wake and sit still before the dream fades

effects.log: A few stalls, a barrow of pears, a woman laughing. They mean something you cannot say.

choices.text: Write down the prices at the market

effects.log: Nonsense, you think. Later, you see they were a formula.

events.text: The Dao does not explain itself, but it does hint. Today, the hint is how quickly the kettle boils when you stop watching it.

choices.text: Stop watching the kettle

effects.log: It boils. You think of other things. Something else boils too, a thing long on the simmer.

choices.text: Watch the kettle and be wrong on purpose

effects.log: It boils at the same speed. You learn the wrongness is yours.

events.text: You realise, mid-sentence, that you have been trying to grasp the Dao the way one grasps water, with a clenched hand. You open the hand, and are wet to the wrist.

choices.text: Open the hand and stay wet

effects.log: You are wet to the wrist and happy. The water, such as it is, stays.

choices.text: Dry your hand and try again with a bowl

effects.log: A bowl is an honest vessel. The Dao fits it, a little.

events.text: At this height the Dao is less a teaching than a weather. It has fronts, pressures, seasons. You learn to read its sky as a fisherman reads his own coast.

choices.text: Read the sky of it for a season

effects.log: You keep a weather-diary of insight. In winter it has a front, a calm, a rain.

choices.text: Set a sail on it and drift

effects.log: A small sail of intention. You are carried to a coast you cannot name.

events.text: A moment of comprehension comes with no sensation at all: at one breath you did not understand, and at the next you had always understood.

choices.text: Sit in the always-had-understood

effects.log: It is like being born at the same moment as the sun. You rest a long while.

choices.text: Ask what you understood

effects.log: A quiet sentence. You lose it at once and keep the feeling.

events.text: The Dao reveals a single small rule and hides the rest. You test the rule against a hundred cases, and it holds in all, and your amazement is quiet and complete.

choices.text: Test the small rule a hundred more times

effects.log: It holds. And you notice the hundred-and-first case is a crack, and the rule is a door.

choices.text: Leave the rule unexamined

effects.log: A gift, held lightly. It works better when not looked at.

events.text: You touch the Dao at the edge of your being, where self thins out into everything. It is neither warm nor cold. It is exactly as large as you let it be.

choices.text: Be exactly as large as it lets you

effects.log: You are nearly the size of the sky. The sensation fades, and the size remains.

choices.text: Draw back from the edge, gently

effects.log: No harm. The edge is not an enemy. You wave to it from the bank.

choices.text: Say thank you to the neither-warm-nor-cold

effects.log: A courteous nothing. Something answers: not a word, a lean toward you.

events.text: Your qi follows your heart, you discover, as a faithful dog follows its owner. When you are quiet the qi lies down at your feet. When you are anxious it pants and circles.

choices.text: Lie down with the qi at your feet

effects.log: It sleeps. You sleep. The first untroubled night in a month.

choices.text: Walk the panting qi around the isle

effects.log: A circuit and a half, and it falls into step with you.

events.text: You are angry at something small. Your qi is angry too, and curdles. The heart is a thermostat, and today it is set too high.

choices.text: Cool the thermostat with a cup of mint

effects.log: A tiny practical remedy. The temper eases.

choices.text: Find out what the small thing really is

effects.log: It is not small, it is old. You nod at it. It settles, a little.

choices.text: Let the qi curdle and see what separates

effects.log: A bitter lesson, true. You skim the top and drink the rest.

events.text: A moment of unexpected kindness on the White Stairs warms the heart, and the qi rises through the golden core like sap in spring, unforced and good.

choices.text: Remember the kindness for a week

effects.log: The warmth keeps. Your qi runs sweet until the next new moon.

choices.text: Return the kindness to someone else

effects.log: A gift passed on is a gift doubled. The stair, you note, is warmer still.

events.text: You notice that your qi runs smoothest when you are grateful. You test this with a cheap gratitude, and it fails. You test it with a true one, and it works at once.

choices.text: Practise the true gratitude daily

effects.log: A true one, each dawn. Within a season the qi is a river.

choices.text: Catch the cheap gratitude when it comes

effects.log: You see its small, polished face and forgive it.

events.text: The heart is a lake. The qi is the wind across it. You may not command the wind, but you can clear the lake of reeds until the wind passes over without a catch.

choices.text: Clear one reed a day

effects.log: A year of reeds. The wind, at last, crosses the lake in a single clear stroke.

choices.text: Sit by the lake and ask nothing of the wind

effects.log: It comes anyway, as it does to those who stop calling it.

choices.text: Cut a path through the reeds for a friend

effects.log: They wade in, laughing, and the lake, as a favour, smooths.

events.text: Grief opens a door in the heart, and the qi walks through into a room you have never entered. It is an odd, empty, clean room, and you are in no hurry to leave.

choices.text: Stay in the empty room

effects.log: It is odd and clean. You furnish it with a single stool and sit.

choices.text: Invite someone in

effects.log: A shy guest, a kettle. The room becomes a room.

choices.text: Leave and close the door softly

effects.log: A small grief, honoured. You come back in spring.

events.text: You attempt a mind-clearing technique and find that what you must clear is not thought but a kind of worry, which has been there so long it feels like furniture.

choices.text: Name the worry and set it on the table

effects.log: It is smaller than the table. You drink tea beside it.

choices.text: Sweep the furniture out and keep only the chair

effects.log: A bare room of the mind. Light fills it quickly.

events.text: A long walk along the isle's edge, no destination, and by the end the heart and qi are in step. It was the simplest thing, and it took you three hundred years to try.

choices.text: Walk the edge again tomorrow

effects.log: Another circuit, another mild bliss. The three hundred years begin to look forgivable.

choices.text: Tell someone how simple it was

effects.log: They laugh with relief, and set off on their own walk.

events.text: Your heart, at this height, is so large and still that your qi moves in it like a swimmer in the open sea: no walls to strike, and no fear of the depth.

choices.text: Swim in the open sea

effects.log: No walls, no fear. The qi is a long clean stroke from horizon to horizon.

choices.text: Float on your back and look up

effects.log: The sky is the lid of a very large cup. You are content in it.

events.text: At last the heart and qi are not two things but one tide, rising and falling with each other. You can no longer say which leads, and you no longer need to.

choices.text: Stop asking which leads

effects.log: A final unclenching. The tide rises and falls, and so do you.

choices.text: Mark the moment with a bowl of plain rice

effects.log: A small ceremony of the ordinary. It tastes of everything.

choices.text: Teach no one, and live it

effects.log: The quietest lesson. Those who look at you learn it anyway.

events.text: The tempering fire at the Nine Clouds is not red but white-gold, and burns without wood. You enter it to the shoulders and your bones sing a single clear note.

choices.text: Enter to the neck

effects.log: The note rises to a hum in the skull. You come out ringing, grinning, and a little dizzy.

choices.text: Stay at the shoulders and listen

effects.log: A single clear note, held. Your bones learn it by heart.

events.text: The immortal flame touches only what is impure in you. You come out lighter by a handful of old griefs you did not know you carried, and your skin tingles.

choices.text: Let the flame take the old griefs

effects.log: They go like smoke. A handful is missing and, oddly, you do not mind.

choices.text: Hold back one grief and keep it

effects.log: A small stone you choose to carry. The flame honours the choice.

events.text: You temper your forearms this season. The flame wraps them like a cloth and withdraws, and they are, for a time, as light and as hard as bamboo.

choices.text: Wear the bamboo light a few days

effects.log: Light and hard, and a trifle brittle. You learn to move around it.

choices.text: Temper the other forearm next season

effects.log: A balanced pair. The left arm is jealous for a week.

events.text: The fire asks that you not flinch. You do, a little. It waits, politely, until you stop, and then continues, and neither of you mentions it.

choices.text: Hold still, and let the flinch pass

effects.log: The fire waits. When you stop flinching it resumes, and there is no shame.

choices.text: Hum while it works

effects.log: A modest tune. The fire, delighted, picks a harmony.

events.text: A fire-keeper at the Nine Clouds watches you through the lattice and says, in the voice of a woman reading a tide-table, that you have another quarter-hour in you. She is right.

choices.text: Take the quarter-hour as she says

effects.log: Exactly right. You step out and she is already writing the next appointment.

choices.text: Ask the fire-keeper how she knows

effects.log: 'I have watched ten thousand,' she says. 'It is always the same face.' You see yourself in it.

events.text: The flame hums a note through your marrow. You hold it with your breath and feel the bones take it in, one by one, a chord arranging itself.

choices.text: Hold the chord and let it settle

effects.log: One bone at a time. The chord resolves in the tibia, and you laugh aloud.

choices.text: Sing the note back to the fire

effects.log: The fire dims, politely, for an instant. Then it burns brighter.

events.text: In the fire you see the injuries of the centuries as faint rivers on your inner skin. The flame redraws them as veins of jade.

choices.text: Read the rivers of old injuries

effects.log: A map of falls and blows and slights. Each has a name you can still say.

choices.text: Thank the jade veins

effects.log: A quiet gratitude, to a body that has done its work.

events.text: The immortal fire is older than the isle, and it tempers with the patience of something that has all the time. You offer it all of yours in return.

choices.text: Offer the time in return

effects.log: The fire, accepting, takes a little of it. Tomorrow you are patient to the bone.

choices.text: Sit by the fire without entering

effects.log: A companionable evening. The flame and you agree on the weather.

events.text: You pass through the flame and out the far side, and it is as if you have stepped from one room of your body into the next, larger, brighter, with the windows open.

choices.text: Step back into the first room to say goodbye

effects.log: The old room is small and warm. You close the door and leave it lit.

choices.text: Open the windows of the new room wider

effects.log: Wind and light. The body breathes through all its panes.

events.text: The fire, at your standing, no longer burns. It recognises. You pass through it like an old friend through a familiar door, and it trims your edges as you go.

choices.text: Let the fire trim your edges

effects.log: A fine precise snipping. You come out neater by a degree, and no less yourself.

choices.text: Greet the fire by its oldest name

effects.log: It flares, in welcome. Between you there is no need for the rest.

choices.text: Pass through at a walk, not a stride

effects.log: A small difference. The fire notes it with a sort of tenderness.

events.text: The sword form you have practised since childhood has a first movement, a plain upward draw. At this height the draw takes a full hour and the whole cloud-court bends with it.

choices.text: Draw it again, an hour long, and watch the court bend

effects.log: The tiles ring. You and the cloud-court agree on the length of a breath.

choices.text: Draw it small, and see what remains

effects.log: A hand-span draw, tiny and exact. It is the same stroke, and you are astonished.

events.text: Your palm strike, scaled to an immortal's body, stirs the sea of clouds a mile below. You hold back, and even so a cormorant tumbles in the backwash.

choices.text: Hold back further and spare the cormorant

effects.log: A softer palm still stirs the sea. The bird flies off, unharmed and indignant.

choices.text: Strike once into the open sea and listen

effects.log: A long grey echo comes back. You learn the shape of the distance.

choices.text: Teach the palm to stir only a cup of tea

effects.log: A small, perfect ripple. You drink it.

events.text: You attempt the Hundred-Lotus formation on a platform of cloud. The first lotus holds for an hour. By the tenth the pattern dissolves like breath on glass.

choices.text: Let the pattern dissolve and re-draw it

effects.log: On the second try nine lotuses hold, and the tenth waits kindly.

choices.text: Practise on a single lotus for a month

effects.log: A patient flower. Held long enough, it blooms on its own.

events.text: A sword drawn at immortal scale does not cut; it removes the idea of the thing. You test it on a leaf and the leaf, politely, is not there.

choices.text: Cut a thought instead of a leaf

effects.log: The thought, too, is not there. A relief, then a small hole, then a view.

choices.text: Sheathe it and let the leaf live

effects.log: The leaf turns in the air, unconcerned. Restraint is its own art.

events.text: The old palm form has a gentle second movement, a pushing-aside. Performed with the weight of a floating isle behind it, it clears a whole bank of mist.

choices.text: Clear the mist and then bring it back

effects.log: A sigh in the valley as it returns. The weight of the isle is a lesson in gentleness.

choices.text: Use the push-aside on a worry

effects.log: It moves. The worry goes round the corner, to be dealt with later, and the room is calm.

events.text: You teach your sword to say less. The less it says the more it means, until the form is a single line of stillness.

choices.text: Teach it to say only what is needed

effects.log: Seven words become three. Three become one stroke. You stop there.

choices.text: Let it say the extra and keep the silence after

effects.log: The pause after the stroke is longer than the stroke. It is the better half.

events.text: Formation work at this scale is a kind of gardening: you lay down the pattern and then wait for it to grow into the sky. Yours grows slowly, like a bamboo grove.

choices.text: Plant the pattern and wait a year

effects.log: A small shoot in the sky. It gives shade to nothing and pleasure to many.

choices.text: Prune it at the first sign of pride

effects.log: A neat cut. The grove remains modest and tall.

events.text: The sword and the palm stop being two arts and become one gesture with two hands. You have no name for it. It rains on your isle for a day, and you stand in the rain.

choices.text: Stand in the rain and make no gesture

effects.log: The rain takes the gesture you did not make. It runs off your sleeves in a clean line.

choices.text: Name the gesture 'Two Hands'

effects.log: A plain name, perfect for it. It works better named.

events.text: The art no longer reaches outward. It turns, now, and goes in, and what it cuts is the last small vanity of the cutter.

choices.text: Cut the vanity gently

effects.log: It comes away, thin as a petal. You are lighter by exactly the weight of a compliment.

choices.text: Let the art turn and stay turned

effects.log: Inward, it is quiet. You find a good deal of furniture to rearrange.

choices.text: Practise outward again, in remembrance

effects.log: A bright, bold swing. A grin follows. Not every art need be wise.

events.text: At the summit the art is almost motionless: one breath, one step, one stroke, and it holds the sky up for a heartbeat before the world begins again.

choices.text: Hold the sky up for the full heartbeat

effects.log: A long, serious second. The world then resumes, and thanks you without knowing.

choices.text: Let the heartbeat pass and move on

effects.log: Some strokes are for the sky alone. You bow and walk away.

choices.text: Teach the stillness to a pupil by sitting beside them

effects.log: They sit. They do not move. By evening they have learned the whole art.

events.text: You still wake at the hour a mortal farmer would, though you have not needed sleep in an age. The habit is a rope to the village you came from, and you let it hold.

choices.text: Wake with the farmer and watch the dawn

effects.log: A cold bright sky and a faint smell of woodsmoke from nowhere. You laugh, remembering.

choices.text: Sleep in, for once, and let the rope go slack

effects.log: A soft, long rest. The rope waits, unoffended.

events.text: Out of habit you check your sleeves for a purse that no longer exists. Immortals have no use for coin, and you find it oddly moving to be so unburdened.

choices.text: Reach for the purse and find a stone instead

effects.log: A smooth pebble from your sleeve. It does as well as coin.

choices.text: Laugh at your own hands

effects.log: They have been checking a long time. They are kind hands.

choices.text: Give the empty-purse feeling a small bow

effects.log: The old worry thanks you, and goes.

events.text: You catch yourself rationing food you do not need, a relic of a hungry childhood. You sit and eat a full bowl slowly, in apology to the child.

choices.text: Eat the bowl slowly and thank the child

effects.log: Rice, pickle, steam. The child inside sits down and eats too.

choices.text: Share the bowl with a hungry neighbour

effects.log: A small custom, honoured. The neighbour pays you back with a story.

events.text: Your old guarded way of sitting, back to a wall, eyes on the door, has no use here. You turn your cushion to face the open sky and feel the world widen.

choices.text: Face the sky and sit

effects.log: The back unclenches. The sky is not a door but a field.

choices.text: Keep the wall for bad days

effects.log: A choice. On some evenings you still need a wall.

events.text: A mortal habit of haggling still springs up in you whenever a gift is offered. You stifle it with some effort and receive the gift plainly.

choices.text: Receive the gift plainly and say thank you

effects.log: It is awkward and lovely. The giver glows.

choices.text: Haggle, just once, for old times

effects.log: The giver laughs. The two of you settle on a pot of tea.

events.text: You keep a small bowl of rice by the window for ancestors long past thanking. Here in the clouds the gesture seems quaint, and also the truest thing you do all day.

choices.text: Fill the bowl each dawn and speak to the names

effects.log: Names, a few. The window listens. Something eases in your chest.

choices.text: Teach the custom to a neighbour

effects.log: A quiet bowl appears on the next isle. The custom travels.

events.text: The old habit of looking behind you lingers. No enemy has followed you up here in a thousand years. Still, you look, and then you smile at your own shadow.

choices.text: Turn and look, and smile at your shadow

effects.log: It smiles back, a trifle late. You both feel foolish and well.

choices.text: Stop looking behind you for a year

effects.log: A long unpicking of a long habit. The neck relaxes and so do other things.

events.text: You hum a village song while you cultivate. The air of the Upper Realm was not made for it, and yet it hums back, a note lower, in your own bones.

choices.text: Hum a verse softly into the cloud

effects.log: The air hums the bass. A passing crane tilts its head.

choices.text: Teach the song to a young immortal

effects.log: They learn it by ear and mispronounce a word. The mistake is lovely.

events.text: A mortal's rush to be early is the last of your habits that bothers anyone. A rival remarks that you arrived at a feast before the lanterns were lit.

choices.text: Arrive early on purpose and wait for the lanterns

effects.log: You watch the lights come on one by one. The rival finally appears, and finds you serene.

choices.text: Arrive exactly on time, to spare the rival

effects.log: Courtesy, uncomfortably precise. Both of you notice, and say nothing.

events.text: The last of your mortal habits is a simple thing: you still say thank you to doors. You hold that this will be the final thing to leave you, and the best.

choices.text: Thank every door today

effects.log: Twelve doors, twelve thanks. Evening is warmer than it has any reason to be.

choices.text: Let the habit go the way it came, unseen

effects.log: One day you find you did not say it. You say it twice the next.

choices.text: Teach the doors to say it back

effects.log: A small, silly spell. Two hinges creak a pleased note.

events.text: A hundred years ago you sat in this exact place and wished for the next gate. Today you do the same, and find the wish unchanged. You laugh softly at the loyalty of it.

choices.text: Say the wish aloud and let it be the same

effects.log: It hangs in the air like an old coat. You put it on and sit.

choices.text: Revise the wish by a single word

effects.log: A small mend. The gate, you suspect, noticed.

events.text: The sun comes up. The mist rolls back. You were here for the thousand dawns before this one and will be for the thousand after. That, you notice, is a kind of belonging.

choices.text: Count the dawns as a gift

effects.log: Every one unrepeated, though identical. You start counting again and lose track gladly.

choices.text: Greet the sun by name

effects.log: The first thing you have named in an age. It is not a bad name.

events.text: There is a small thing you have always done with your left hand when you think: a tap, two, then a pause. Someone you loved did it too. You do it still, a long way from them.

choices.text: Tap twice and pause on purpose

effects.log: The pause is a small room. You furnish it with a memory and sit in it.

choices.text: Teach the tap to a friend without telling them why

effects.log: A quiet inheritance. They find it in their hands months later.

events.text: Whole civilisations have risen and fallen in the mortal world, and the way you tie your sash has not altered since the age of eleven.

choices.text: Tie the sash the old way and smile

effects.log: Eleven years old, in a village, in a sash. It is the same sash.

choices.text: Tie it a new way for a day

effects.log: It feels like betrayal and freedom. The old way is waiting at dusk.

events.text: The same question has stood at the edge of your attention since you were young, patient as a heron: what is it for? You are no nearer an answer, and perhaps nearer the question.

choices.text: Let the heron wait

effects.log: The question stays, patient, elegant. You do not shoo it.

choices.text: Ask the question in a new key

effects.log: It sounds different. You do not get the answer, but the key is a gift.

choices.text: Ask the question of a child

effects.log: The child answers at once, wrongly, perfectly. You are silent.

events.text: The tea is cold again. It always is by the time you remember it. Some constants are a comfort and a joke at once.

choices.text: Reheat the tea and drink it slowly

effects.log: It is better warm. The joke still stands.

choices.text: Drink it cold with a smile

effects.log: It is bitter and exact. You laugh at yourself, quietly.

events.text: At the end of each day you look up at the same few stars from the same few places, and each year they are a little more like old companions than old facts.

choices.text: Greet the stars as companions

effects.log: Each has a nickname. They have not objected.

choices.text: Learn a new constellation

effects.log: A small outing for the mind. The old stars are jealous.

events.text: You find in yourself the exact tilt of head you had at your first lesson. A hundred teachers have not removed it. You are, you decide, glad.

choices.text: Tilt your head on purpose and sit

effects.log: The lesson, again, from the start. You are very patient with the beginner.

choices.text: Straighten up and see what changes

effects.log: A hundred teachers would be proud. A hundred teachers, you suspect, would also be amused.

events.text: The thing that remains, as every other thing is shed, is a kind of attention. It has no features and is quite unmistakable. You would know it anywhere in the dark.

choices.text: Be the attention for an hour

effects.log: No features, no history, no wish. A good, bright hour.

choices.text: Call it by a name of your own

effects.log: A funny little name. The attention answers to it.

choices.text: Let it be unnamed and unwatched

effects.log: It stays in the dark and keeps the house.

events.text: Beneath the Dao, beneath the gate, beneath all of it, you are the same attentive person you were on the first morning. This does not disappoint you. It rests you.

choices.text: Rest in the sameness

effects.log: It is the largest thing you have known, and the easiest to carry.

choices.text: Tell the first morning that you are still here

effects.log: Across the ages, a small, attentive thing waves back.

choices.text: Make a cup of tea and sit with the person you were

effects.log: They have questions. You have, for once, answers.

events.text: An alchemist of the Nine Clouds offers you a settling pill, the kind that smooths a young immortal's qi like a hand over a rumpled sheet. It tastes of rain on pine.

choices.text: Take it and sit

effects.log: The pill sinks and spreads. For a week your foundation feels freshly swept.

choices.text: Ask what it costs the maker

effects.log: The alchemist is surprised to be asked. A year of fire-tending, she says, and smiles. You send her a jar of honey.

events.text: On the coldest night of the upper year the isle frosts over and your breath hangs in the air like a pale ghost. Cultivating in it is hard, and, you suspect, good for you.

choices.text: Sit bare-handed in the frost

effects.log: The cold gets in and out again. By dawn you are clear as glass and your fingers feel like a stranger found them.

choices.text: Light a lamp and meditate beside it

effects.log: A small flame, a long hour. The warmth makes room in you for a quiet you did not know was missing.

events.text: Each year the isles hang paper lanterns for the Night of Returned Qi. You hang one for the self who first reached the clouds, who is long gone and not lost.

choices.text: Write a line on it for them

effects.log: The ink dries as you watch. The lantern rises and the line goes with it into the dark.

choices.text: Hang it blank

effects.log: Some things are better said without words. The lantern burns steadily until dawn.

events.text: A rival of your own rung challenges you to a bout of forms, not a fight: each shows the other the best of what they have. The challenger's palm is better than you expected.

choices.text: Match them form for form

effects.log: It is a long afternoon. You lose by a hair, and the hair is a lesson you could not have bought.

choices.text: Show them what you would not show a stranger

effects.log: The challenger goes quiet. Then they bow, a real bow. You have given up a secret and gained a witness.

choices.text: Decline politely and offer tea

effects.log: They laugh, and sit, and talk until dusk. It turns out you have been rivals mostly out of habit.

events.text: You tend a small garden of spirit herbs beside your cushion. A crisp-leaved sprout is trying to bloom out of season, and you cannot decide whether to let it.

choices.text: Let it bloom early

effects.log: It opens, one pale flower, and dies by evening. The fragrance lingers on your sleeve for a week, and in your qi for longer.

choices.text: Shelter it until its season

effects.log: You build a small screen of paper. It blooms in time, fuller than any you have grown.

events.text: A pilgrim climbs the White Stairs on their knees, mumbling a long prayer. You have not heard a prayer in so long that the sound strikes you like a bell in a cellar.

choices.text: Climb beside them and match their pace

effects.log: It takes half a day. At the top they weep and thank you, and you say that they did it themselves.

choices.text: Whisper a blessing from the air

effects.log: The pilgrim looks up with sudden joy. You did not mean it as more than courtesy, and it works more than courtesy.

events.text: A storm builds over the Sea of Clouds, the dry white kind with no rain. You climb to the roof and watch it, because lightning is the great teacher of those who mean to cross a gate.

choices.text: Meet a bolt with your open palm

effects.log: The bolt arrives, takes your measure, and leaves. Your hand tingles for a week and your qi runs hot and clean.

choices.text: Count the gaps between flashes

effects.log: You learn the storm has a rhythm, as all storms do. You will not forget its tempo on the day it counts.

choices.text: Go inside and ward the windows

effects.log: Sensible, humble, correct. You sleep to the thunder like a child, and wake rested.

events.text: A hermit at the edge of the isles asks to borrow a cloud method of yours, only to copy. They have the look of someone who has lost a great deal and would like it not to be wasted.

choices.text: Lend it freely

effects.log: They return it in a month with a note of thanks and a pressed flower. Your method was improved a little in the copying.

choices.text: Teach it in person instead

effects.log: It takes three weeks. You teach them what the page cannot say, and discover that you did not know it either until you said it aloud.

events.text: You sleep, for the first time in decades, by choice. The dream you have is of a field after rain, and when you wake your qi is laid out like a field too.

choices.text: Lie still and let the dream finish

effects.log: It finishes. A little quiet joy lingers all day, and your meridians seem to have been rinsed.

choices.text: Rise and write the dream down

effects.log: It reads as nonsense, and then, on the third reading, as instruction.

events.text: A Star Sea Pavilion envoy visits your isle and, with studied courtesy, offers a reading of your cultivation's future. They will not name a price. They never do.

choices.text: Accept and listen

effects.log: She reads a chart, frowns, smiles, frowns again. What she tells you is true in a way you cannot use until later.

choices.text: Decline, and give her tea

effects.log: She is pleased to be refused. She leaves a small star-chart as a gift, unasked.

events.text: A spirit stone is missing from the array. A young servant of the isle, red with shame, confesses they took it to ease a sick sister on the lower isles.

choices.text: Let it pass and send a second stone with them

effects.log: They weep. You pretend to study a scroll. Weeks later the sister walks the stairs on her own legs.

choices.text: Teach them a breathing method instead

effects.log: It is cheaper than a stone and better. They go, bowing, with a way to heal themselves.

choices.text: Have the stone returned and say nothing

effects.log: Order is kept. A cold little knot remains in your chest, and your qi stumbles over it for days.

events.text: The Jade Court holds its decennial reading of the methods, a quiet examination of the cultivation of every house. You are invited to sit as a witness, not a judge.

choices.text: Sit and listen to every house

effects.log: Nine days of gentle argument. By the end you can see how wide and how particular the path is.

choices.text: Slip out to walk the terraces

effects.log: You miss the formal bits and find a quiet corner where an old archivist is feeding sparrows. You learn more from her.

events.text: You grind ink for an hour, as you have for centuries, and the ink tells you your mood before you do. Today it is thick and restless.

choices.text: Write a long, slow character, again and again

effects.log: By the fiftieth, the restlessness is gone. By the hundredth, the character has become a face.

choices.text: Pour the ink out onto the cloud-water

effects.log: It spreads and thins and vanishes. You laugh, and your shoulders drop an inch.

events.text: Through a rare gap in the sea of clouds you glimpse the mortal land: a tiny river, a tiny bridge, a tiny cart. You cultivate by looking at it for a week.

choices.text: Watch until a single life comes clear

effects.log: A cart-driver, perhaps. Late at night, a woman waving from a window. You sit with them as a god of nothing, and it humbles you well.

choices.text: Close the gap before you grow sentimental

effects.log: The cloud closes. You carry the cart, the bridge and the river with you anyway.

events.text: A neighbouring immortal plays a bone flute at dusk, always the same four notes, never the fifth. You find yourself waiting for the fifth, every evening.

choices.text: Walk over and ask about the fifth note

effects.log: They smile and say it is a joke between them and a friend who is gone. You sit and listen to the four notes together.

choices.text: Hum the fifth yourself from your terrace

effects.log: The flute pauses. Then, softly, the fifth note answers. Some things heal by being finished.

events.text: A rope bridge of cloud-silk joins your isle to the next. It sways when you cross, and today it hums, as if the isle on the far side is trying to say something.

choices.text: Cross slowly and listen

effects.log: Halfway you hear it: a faint, low bell. You return with a new question.

choices.text: Run the length of it and laugh

effects.log: You arrive breathless, lighter, and as if ten years younger. The bridge holds.

events.text: In a long meditation you meet, in dream, a teacher from the mortal land, long dead. They sit at the other side of your cushion and criticise your posture, as they always did.

choices.text: Take the criticism and straighten

effects.log: It is an old, loving rebuke. You wake with your back set right and your eyes damp.

choices.text: Ask what they would say of your path now

effects.log: They are silent a long time. Then they say, very gently, that you have gone farther than they hoped, and not so far as you fear.

events.text: A cloud draft knocks a lamp over in your study, and the oldest of your scrolls is singed. You put it out with your sleeve and sit among the ruined pages.

choices.text: Copy what survives by hand, line by line

effects.log: It takes a month. The copy is shaky and honest, and in the copying you find a margin note you had never noticed.

choices.text: Bring the singed scroll to the archivists

effects.log: They treat it with oil and patience. You are told it will last another thousand years, and that you are a careless fool, in that order.

events.text: A wandering immortal, thin as a reed and lit from within, stops at your gate for water. They ask nothing, and carry nothing, and have the look of someone who has finished something.

choices.text: Offer your best tea and listen

effects.log: They tell no stories. They simply sit, and by the second cup you have stopped trying to want anything.

choices.text: Ask the one question you most fear

effects.log: They answer in a sentence of three words. It will take you a century to unpack, and you are grateful already.

events.text: At dawn the rising sun strikes the array at exactly the right angle and the whole pattern lights up, a rare thing. You sit at the centre, grateful for being early.

choices.text: Breathe in as the light rises

effects.log: It is a moment of perfect fit. The qi comes in clean and the foundation takes it like a well takes rain.

choices.text: Trace the light across the lines

effects.log: You see the pattern as a clock, and can read, for the first time, the time it was built to tell.

events.text: A young immortal on the stairs asks, with disarming frankness, whether it ever gets easier. They look tired in the way only the well-intentioned are.

choices.text: Tell them the truth

effects.log: You say it gets different, and that different is a kind of easier. They nod as if you had cured something.

choices.text: Tell them a story instead

effects.log: A long one, half invented. At its end they laugh, and you realise you, too, needed the telling.

events.text: A Jade Void elder offers to show you the First Cut, the sword stroke that precedes every other. The demonstration takes a breath. The memory of it takes a decade.

choices.text: Watch with total attention

effects.log: You do not blink. The stroke is simple, impossible, and now yours to carry. Your sword hand aches in gratitude.

choices.text: Ask them to do it slowly

effects.log: They do. It is, if anything, more terrible slowly, and more instructive.

events.text: Near the upper gates, the atmosphere changes. Time stretches. A week is a breath; a breath is an age. You learn to cultivate in two tempi at once, and are at first quite dizzy.

choices.text: Match the slower tempo

effects.log: You sink into it like a stone into a deep pond. Whole seasons wash through you as ripples.

choices.text: Hold both tempi at once

effects.log: It is nearly impossible, and you manage it for almost a minute. In that minute you see more than in the last century.

events.text: Your cloud-silk robes have worn thin at the cuffs. You sew them yourself, which an immortal need not, in tiny stitches that grow evenly and quietly across the evening.

choices.text: Finish the mending and wear them proud

effects.log: You walk the stairs in the mended robes, and an old gatekeeper nods approval.

choices.text: Sew a small charm into the hem

effects.log: No one will know. You will.

events.text: In the long hush you notice a quiet greed in yourself: a hunger for the next rung that has grown into a kind of appetite. It does not care what it eats.

choices.text: Name it and sit with it

effects.log: Named, it shrinks to the size of a house cat. You feed it a little patience and it purrs.

choices.text: Starve it for a season

effects.log: A hard season, a clear one. When the hunger returns it is milder, and you are the master of the table.

events.text: A dying immortal of a lower isle sends you their cloud method and a note: 'I kept it for the right person. Do not let it go to the wrong one. Do not let it rot, either.'

choices.text: Take the method and honour the request

effects.log: You read it with care, and make a copy for each of three promising students. The note goes in your sleeve.

choices.text: Sit with the note a long while before reading further

effects.log: Some weights deserve a pause. When you open the scroll it falls open like a flower.

events.text: There is a bird that chatters on your roof every morning, loudly, with no sense of rank. You have been annoyed by it for weeks.

choices.text: Bring it seeds and make peace

effects.log: It comes to your sill and eats from your hand. Your annoyance dissolves, and your qi follows the dissolution.

choices.text: Treat the chatter as a drum for your breath

effects.log: Within the week the bird is a metronome and you are a better sitter for it.

events.text: A ship of cloud-wood drifts to your isle, captained by a smiling immortal who deals in recipes and rumours. They offer a berth for a season of travel and conversation.

choices.text: Board and see the isles

effects.log: A season of strange tea, stranger arguments, and thin air. You come home with twenty questions and no regrets.

choices.text: Stay and trade rumours at the rail

effects.log: You get a handful of true ones, and tell a few of your own.

events.text: The mirror-pool on the south slope has not rippled in years, and today a single drop falls into it from the roof. The rings go out and out and do not return.

choices.text: Watch them to the very edge

effects.log: They fade at the stone rim, at last, and you carry the quiet of that fading for the rest of the day.

choices.text: Drop another one, deliberately

effects.log: The rings meet the old ones. The pattern is cleverer than either, and you sketch it before it closes.

events.text: A younger immortal asks you to spot the flaw in their foundation, as one asks a doctor for a pulse. You see it at once. It is the same flaw you once had.

choices.text: Tell them gently and show your own scar

effects.log: They look at you differently after. The telling mends something in you, too.

choices.text: Hint at it and let them find it

effects.log: It takes them a year. They come back, puffed up and glowing, and you pretend surprise.

events.text: Your cup is chipped on one side, from an accident long ago. You drink from the whole side every morning, and have long since stopped seeing the chip.

choices.text: Mend it with gold lacquer

effects.log: You make a seam of gold along the chip. It is better than new, and you drink to the maker of such things.

choices.text: Leave it as it is

effects.log: The chip is a map of a day you would not give back. You hold it a little more carefully.

events.text: A shrine to a minor immortal of your house stands on the edge of your isle, untended for a century. Moss has filled the eyes of the stone figure.

choices.text: Clean it and burn a stick of incense

effects.log: The moss comes away. The figure looks younger and a little embarrassed. A light wind rises, soft as a nod.

choices.text: Study the inscription on its base

effects.log: The old characters speak of patience and are signed, in a tiny hand, with the name of a famous master.

events.text: You notice that you have been quietly borrowing time, a day here, a year there, against the next gate. The books have not been balanced in a very long while.

choices.text: Pay it back in a season of plain sitting

effects.log: No gate, no push. The ledger evens. You feel an unexpected weight lift off your shoulders.

choices.text: Admit the debt and keep borrowing

effects.log: Honest, at least. The qi gathers in thin interest, and you keep a wary eye on the due date.

events.text: An elder of the Eight Houses sends a High-grade stone as a gift, with a note that it is merely courtesy. You know no courtesy of this size is merely anything.

choices.text: Accept and send a modest return

effects.log: A simple scroll of your own notes. It is received with great politeness and fewer strings than feared.

choices.text: Return the stone with thanks

effects.log: The elder is offended, then amused. Respect, later, in small ways, accrues.

choices.text: Use it to deepen your foundation and say so openly

effects.log: You sit for a month with it. The foundation drinks it down. You write a candid letter of thanks and it is well received.

events.text: In the high stillness you hear an echo of your own earliest breath, from the day you first sat to cultivate. It is small, ragged, brave. It is the origin of everything since.

choices.text: Greet it as a child and take its hand

effects.log: The echo quiets. The foundation seems to lean toward it, as a tree toward its seed.

choices.text: Keep the echo as a compass

effects.log: You note its direction. For a century to come you will steer by it.

events.text: At this height a cultivator's every gesture is large. You raise your hand and a cloud-bank moves. You learn, again, the courtesy of the small, and practise the art of doing less.

choices.text: Move only your little finger for a month

effects.log: Absurd, exacting, wonderful. The world answers the finger with equal gravity.

choices.text: Walk through the isle as a mortal would, touching nothing

effects.log: You bump into a table, apologise to it, and laugh. It is the most restful week of the century.

events.text: You are asked to witness another immortal's attempt on the gate, as their second, with a bowl of tea and a calm face. Their hands shake slightly as they take their seat.

choices.text: Sit with them, steady and present

effects.log: They pass. Or they do not. Either way you were there, and the shaking stops when you pour the tea.

choices.text: Study the attempt with a scholar's eye

effects.log: You see an entire grammar of the gate laid bare for an hour. You note it with shaking hands.

events.text: At the upper edge of the sky, light itself seems to thicken. You sit in the last of it and feel that you are near the end of a very long stair, and it has no landing.

choices.text: Sit still and accept the lack of a landing

effects.log: You find that the stair was always the thing. The qi rises in a fine, wide mist and does not trouble to arrive anywhere.

choices.text: Look back down the stair

effects.log: It is very long. Every step is a person you were, and you wave at each one, and each waves back.

events.text: A young immortal from the lower isles stands at your gate with a basket of persimmons and a speech they have clearly rehearsed. They want to learn how to sit. Only that.
events.arc: The Apprentice of the Lower Isle

choices.text: Take the basket and begin

effects.log: You show them the cushion, the breath, the patient emptiness. They are terrible at it. They return the next dawn.

choices.text: Send them to the Scroll Hall instead

effects.log: A kinder no. They go. You half expect to see them again, and you are right to.

events.text: The apprentice has been sitting for years now. Today they ask why you never seem to move. You realise you have forgotten how long it has been since you tried.
events.arc: The Apprentice of the Lower Isle

choices.text: Show them how you moved when young

effects.log: A simple form. They watch with enormous eyes. You are stiff, then loose, then laughing. They are laughing too.

choices.text: Tell them stillness is also movement

effects.log: They try to believe it. It will take years. You enjoy their frown.

events.text: The apprentice sits their own gate attempt, and you serve as their second. They shake. You pour the tea. The sky holds its breath for both of you.
events.arc: The Apprentice of the Lower Isle

choices.text: Steady them with a hand on the shoulder

effects.log: They pass, or half pass. They weep, and you pretend it is the wind. You have rarely been so proud.

choices.text: Stay silent and trust what you taught

effects.log: It is the hardest hour of your century. They come through. You find your own hands are trembling.

events.text: The apprentice, now a peer, brings you a persimmon. 'You taught me to sit,' they say. 'I came to say I think I taught you something too.' They will not say what.
events.arc: The Apprentice of the Lower Isle

choices.text: Ask, and accept whatever they say

effects.log: It is a small, kind, exact thing. You carry it for the rest of the age.

choices.text: Eat the persimmon and say nothing

effects.log: It is sweet and a little astringent, like most true things. They smile. It is enough.

events.text: At a gathering, a retired sword immortal presses a plain blade into your hands and says: 'Hold it for me, will you? Only a while.' Then they walk off, as if to fetch something.

choices.text: Hold it and wait

effects.log: They do not return. The blade is cold, plain, a little heavy. You decide to keep your promise anyway.

choices.text: Practise a form with it while you wait

effects.log: It cuts the clouds as a good sword should, and also seems to be listening.

events.text: The borrowed sword hums at dusk. It has a voice of sorts: a single clear tone, which changes depending on your mood. Tonight it is low and patient.

choices.text: Listen to it every evening

effects.log: You become a student of the sword's patience, which is older than yours.

choices.text: Ask the Jade Void about the retired immortal

effects.log: The archivist goes pale. The immortal left the Void three centuries ago, and no one has seen them since.

events.text: At last the retired immortal returns, thin and radiant, and asks for the sword. 'I wanted to see who it would stay with,' they say. 'You may keep it, if you wish.'

choices.text: Return the sword with thanks

effects.log: They are touched. They leave you a scroll in exchange, with a single stroke on it. It is worth more than the sword.

choices.text: Keep it, and promise to pass it on one day

effects.log: They nod and walk away at once. The sword, in your hands, is now yours and also a promise.

events.text: Years later you hand the borrowed sword to a young swordsman at the Void, with no explanation but the same words: 'Hold it for me, will you?'

choices.text: Watch them walk off with it

effects.log: They are puzzled, then resolved. The tone of the blade changes as they go. The circle closes quietly.

choices.text: Follow and see it hung on a wall

effects.log: It rests in a quiet hall, between two fine ones, plain and perfectly at home.

events.text: You find an array in a cellar of your isle that does nothing. Its lines are flawless, its stones are full, and it simply sits there, gathering and gathering and releasing nothing.

choices.text: Study its design

effects.log: It is a perfect vessel without a mouth. You copy the pattern and wonder who would build a thing so closed.

choices.text: Sit in the middle and see what happens

effects.log: Nothing, for a week. Then a tiny warm bead forms in your golden core and stays.

events.text: The silent array has begun to hum, very faintly, in time with your breath. You suspect it has been learning you, as you learned it.

choices.text: Breathe to its pace for a season

effects.log: You are slowed, deepened, evened. The array glows faintly at the edges.

choices.text: Speak a question into it

effects.log: No answer, but the hum shifts in a way that feels courteous.

events.text: The array opens. Not with a flash, but like a flower: one line unclasps, and then another. Inside, in a small niche, sits a single seed of qi, ancient and unhurried.

choices.text: Take the seed into yourself

effects.log: It warms the whole foundation, quietly, with the weight of something that waited an age for you.

choices.text: Plant it in your garden

effects.log: A pale shoot comes up in spring. It bears no fruit but gives off an air that makes the whole isle quieter.

events.text: A letter arrives by cloud-crane, unsigned, in a hand you almost recognise. It reads: 'I am nearly at the gate. I am afraid. Do you remember how it was?'

choices.text: Write back honestly about your own fear

effects.log: It is the longest letter you have written in an age. The crane is gone before you finish sealing it.

choices.text: Answer with one line of encouragement

effects.log: Brief, warm, true. The crane goes off with a flick.

events.text: A second letter, in a different hand, arrives. 'I failed,' it says. 'I thought I should tell someone who would understand. I do not know why I thought of you.'

choices.text: Write to say you do, and why

effects.log: You explain, without ornament, the thing you learned from your own failure. The crane goes quietly.

choices.text: Send tea and a pressed leaf

effects.log: No words. A leaf from the plum tree, a cup of the leaves. The gesture says what you cannot.

events.text: The third letter comes in a third hand, steady and bright. 'I passed the gate,' it says. 'I wanted you to know. The first letter was from me, and so was the second. I was three people.'

choices.text: Laugh, and reply with a blessing

effects.log: You write: so was I. The crane flies off lighter than it came.

choices.text: Keep all three letters side by side

effects.log: They fit together like three parts of one painting. You hang them in the study.

events.text: An old immortal presents a bill, politely, for a cloud method you learned from them in your youth in the Upper Realm. You had not known it was a loan.

choices.text: Ask what they would like in return

effects.log: They ask for nothing at once. They say they will call it in when the time is right.

choices.text: Offer to teach them something of yours

effects.log: Your old murim palm, in exchange. They are delighted, and you are quietly relieved.

events.text: The old immortal sends for you at last. The debt, it turns out, is a single afternoon of conversation, long overdue, about everything they have forgotten to say.

choices.text: Sit through the afternoon without checking the sun

effects.log: It runs long. You come away tired, full, and richer than you have been in an age.

choices.text: Take notes as they speak

effects.log: Seven pages of crisp memory, a little treasure you will return to often.

events.text: The old immortal passes quietly in their sleep. At the burning, an attendant gives you a scroll: 'The debt is cleared. They wrote that you should keep the method, and pass it on.'

choices.text: Copy the method for the three nearest students

effects.log: It is a tidy act, and a loving one. You feel the old immortal in the pen.

choices.text: Sit with the method and say a quiet thanks

effects.log: The scroll falls open to a passage you have never read, and reads as if they were speaking.
